arxiv-2602-12018:
Language AI offers gains in health, education, governance, and equity, yet its benefits cluster in a handful of languages. Giulia Occhini and twelve co-authors present a global over-time analysis of social, economic, and infrastructural conditions across tongues, assessing deep gaps in language AI. They first map AI resources for 6,003 tongues, finding that dominance by a few tongues is widening divides fast rather than narrowing them.

AI diffusion versus earlier information tools reveals a distinctive hype-driven spread pattern. To guide choices, the authors introduce the Language AI Readiness Index, called EQUATE, mapping tech, social and money, and build needs for AI deployment across tongues. The index highlights places where capacity exists but sits idle, and sets a baseline for a shift toward more lasting and fair language tools.
arxiv-2602-12818:
The same slur can wound as abuse or affirm as in-group speech, depending on who says it and in what context, which makes automated detection genuinely hard. Luca Tedeschini and Matteo Fasulo tackle reclaimed slur detection for the MultiPRIDE shared task, working in Italian and Spanish. Their hierarchical method starts from a simple idea: LGBTQ+ members, on average, use certain slurs in a reclaimed way more often.

First, a weakly supervised language-model step assigns soft community-membership labels from tweets and bios, training a model to learn identity-linked signals. Those signals are then fused with a hate-speech model for the final detection task. Results match a strong baseline statistically, while offering a modular design for adding sociolinguistic context to hate-speech modelling.
arxiv-2602-13218:
Training thinking models from verifiable rewards is bottlenecked by data: expert-written code and fixed templates confine growth to small shifts of current instances. Bowen Liu and four co-authors shift what evolves from problem instances to task-family specifications. Their SSLogic system has language-model agents iteratively authoring and refining executable generator-validator pairs in a generate-validate-refine loop, producing groups carrying new rules and difficulty gradients instead of setting tweaks.

A multi-gate checks protocol combines multi-strategy consensus with adversarial blind review, in which stand-alone agents solve instances through code they write and run, filtering ill-posed tasks before training. Starting with 400 seed groups, two evolution rounds produce 953 groups and 21,389 verifiable instances. Comparisons on external Enigmata data show higher training utility for evolved data, with gains of 5.2 on SynLogic, 3.0 on AIME25, and 5.5 on BBH, plus selective logic and operation gains of 13.2% and 9.6% on KORBench.
arxiv-2602-13418:
Language is increasingly modeled in curved spaces, yet it was unclear whether curvature belongs to text itself or merely to the embedding chosen. This paper argues text truly has curvature and shows how to detect, define, and use it through Texture, a word-level discrete curvature signal native to language. Existence is certified both empirically and theoretically: semantic inference in real corpora is non-flat.

Texture is defined as a signed two-axis curvature of the word-in-context belief field, capturing whether added context from one side focuses or fans out meaning from the other. As a control tool, it improved long-context inference via curvature-guided compression and retrieval-augmented generation via curvature-guided routing. Karish Grover leads the work with four co-authors.
arxiv-2602-13618:
Spin polarization of hyperons and spin alignment of mesons in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC point to a strong vorticity field born in those collisions. This paper offers a second, data-driven route to that field, extracting global vorticity directly from transverse momentum spectra of produced hadrons rather than from polarization alone. Data span lambda, xi, omega, K-star, phi, rho, and D-star hadrons at mid-rapidity in gold-gold and lead-lead collisions across beam energies from 7.7 GeV to 5.02 TeV and many centrality classes.

Extracted vorticity magnitudes agree with values from lambda spin data under thermal models in the slow-motion limit. Notably, vorticity depends strongly on particle species and varies in complex ways with impact class and beam energy, indicating spin-vorticity effects hinge on hadron structure and freeze-out dynamics. Bhagyarathi Sahoo leads the work with two co-authors.
arxiv-2602-14118:
Hatim Ennayar and two co-authors report a 2026 arXiv experiment on drops hitting surfactant-laden thin films. The focus is vortex ring dynamics, traced with bottom- and side-view imaging. Surfactants change how a splash mixes, but the link between surface stresses and ring behavior needed direct evidence.

Raising surfactant concentration steadily stabilized vortex rings, damped azimuthal instabilities, and favored concentric mixing patterns. A regime map in film thickness, Reynolds number, and surface-tension ratio yielded an empirical instability threshold. Shadowgraphy hints that Marangoni stresses reshape early capillary waves, possibly delaying ring breakup. The results clarify how interfacial stresses steer mixing in thin-film impacts.
arxiv-2602-14318:
Trishit Mondal and one co-author ask a 2026 arXiv question: how trusted are transformers? These designs reshaped machine learning, and they now serve high-stakes areas such as health care, self-run systems, climate models, drug finds, nuclear science, and robots. Use at that scale demands strict checks.

The paper reviews trust across clarity, explainability, toughness to hostile attack, fairness, and privacy. It surveys transformer models in safety-key uses spanning language, vision, and science and tech fields, including medicine, earth science, matter science, fluid motion, and nuclear science. The synthesis maps where trust is earned, where it frays, and what proof future claims should carry.
arxiv-2602-14418:
Zizhou Ge and two co-authors set up a 2026 arXiv benchmark for matching UV theories onto Higgs true field theory. Matching the real Higgs triplet model onto HEFT under varied knob choices and power-count plans yields several sample HEFT forms, whose links the paper clears.

The main HEFT, or pHEFT, is offered as the benchmark from which other builds derive step by step. Its knob choice keeps straight links between UV Lagrangian knobs and squared heavy masses. Using inverse squared heavy masses as stretch knobs, with no extra rules, keeps max UV facts and higher perturb exactness. Studies of a Z2-symmetric singlet model and a two-Higgs-doublet model show rules for sound main builds.
arxiv-2602-14618:
Random fields model patterns that vary across space, from magnets to images. J.-R. Chazottes, with two co-authors, studies when such fields show Gaussian concentration, meaning local averages stay tightly bunched. The fields arise as finitary codings of independent inputs.

The main result says concentration survives coding when the coding volume has finite second moment. With a coupling-from-the-past structure, a first moment suffices, and both bounds are sharp. The team applies the result to Gibbs measures and lattice models. For Ising, Potts, and random-cluster models, concentration holds exactly in the full uniqueness regime.
arxiv-2602-14918:
S. Zhang and colleagues model shock physics with physics-informed MeshGraphNets, seeking learning-based surrogates for costly particle-in-cell and hydrodynamic solvers in plasma physics and astrophysics. High-resolution shock simulations strain scalability, so a surrogate that preserves physical fidelity while running faster is prized.

Their PhyMGN model tackles Sedov-Taylor shock propagation on grids, embedding weak physics constraints from the Euler equations via finite differences into a graph network. Self-similar shock structure emerges from learned dynamics guided by physics, not merely fitted to data. Shock-dominated flows gain a faster, physics-aware emulator.
arxiv-2602-15018:
Das and Chaudhari present Neurosim, a fast real-time library for simulating neuromorphic robot perception. It models dynamic vision sensors, RGB cameras, depth sensors, and inertial sensors, plus the agile dynamics of multi-rotor vehicles in complex, changing settings. On a desktop GPU it reaches frame rates near 2700 frames per second.

Neurosim joins a ZeroMQ-based messaging library called Cortex, built for smooth links to machine learning and robotics workflows. Cortex moves messages with high throughput and low latency for Python and C++ programs, with native support for NumPy arrays and PyTorch tensors. The paper shows the pair training perception and control methods on synchronized multimodal data and testing them live in closed loop.
arxiv-2602-15118:
Haide and colleagues build a real-time graph neural network trigger for the Belle II electromagnetic calorimeter at the SuperKEKB collider. The algorithm treats trigger cells as graph nodes for clustering, feature extraction, and signal classification with fixed latency. It predicts cluster positions and energies and scores signals, allowing more flexible grouping than the baseline.

On an FPGA inside the Belle II trigger readout, the system sustains megahertz trigger throughput. Tests on simulated events and collision data show energy resolution comparable to the old trigger. Position sharpness for high-energy clusters improves up to 18 percent centrally. Cluster purity rises up to 20 percent at low energies for isolated clusters. Cluster efficiency improves up to 20 percent for overlapping clusters. The classifier adds background suppression at fixed signal retention. Latency still exceeds the trigger decision budget, but the system runs at full conditions with 100 percent uptime, a first step for FPGA triggers.
arxiv-2602-15618:
Ahmed and colleagues address a practical sensing problem: spotting when terrain material changes in radar images, for instance through shifts in permittivity, roughness, or moisture. They build a light electromagnetic forward model that simulates pairs of single-look complex radar images over time from labelled material maps. On those simulated scenes they derive physics-aware feature stacks, including interferometric coherence.

They test unsupervised detectors on that ground: Reed-Xiaoli and local Reed-Xiaoli with robust scatter estimation, coherent change detection, and a compact convolutional autoencoder. Monte Carlo sweeps vary material change, number of looks, and clutter type at fixed false alarm rate. Coherence and robust covariance markedly improve detection, and a simple score-level fusion wins on F1 in heavy-tailed clutter.
arxiv-2602-15718:
Bello-Hernández and colleagues study how geometric polynomials behave at large degree. They work in the complex plane minus the interval from minus one to zero, and on that range itself. They also measure the gap between consecutive zeros in the bulk of the interval. They prove that the polynomials satisfy certain orthogonality properties.

Because these polynomials relate closely to Eulerian polynomials, the results transfer to the Eulerian case verbatim. The paper thus serves two families at once. Readers of the first family gain asymptotics, zero spacing, and orthogonality. Readers of the second inherit the same results without new proofs.
arxiv-2602-15918:
Xu and colleagues built EarthSpatialBench, a broad test set for spatial skill by multimodal language models on Earth imagery. Such skill has lagged on Earth images. It must ground objects in georeferenced images and judge distances, directions, and topological links from visual cues plus vector shapes such as 2D boxes, polylines, and polygons.

Old Earth imagery tests stress 2D grounding, captioning, and coarse spatial links. They lack exact distance and direction tests, systematic topological links, and complex shapes beyond boxes. EarthSpatialBench holds over 325K question-answer pairs. It spans rough and exact distance and direction work, systematic topological links, and single-object, object-pair, and aggregate group queries. Refs come through text, visual overlays, and explicit geometry. Tests on open and closed models expose clear limits in spatial skill.
arxiv-2602-16318:
Iris van der Giessen and coauthors provide a comprehensive overview of interpolation in proof theory. This survey walks through proof-theoretic methods that settle interpolation properties for logics of four kinds: classical, intuitionistic, modal, and substructural. At the heart of the account sit two basic techniques: the Maehara method for Craig interpolation and the Pitts method for uniform interpolation. The chapter demonstrates how those methods lead to results on well-behaved proof systems in the contemporary framework of universal proof theory.

It also shows how they provide a road map for constructing proofs using modern proof formalisms. Emphasis falls on constructive, modular, and syntax-driven techniques that illuminate deeper connections between interpolation properties and proof systems. For readers in logic, the chapter offers a single entry point to a broad field, showing how two classic methods anchor contemporary work on proof systems.
arxiv-2602-16518:
Mark de Berg and Geert van Wordragen improve bounds for the planar one-round discrete Voronoi game. Two players compete over a set of voters as points in the plane. The first places a set of points, then the second places a set, and each voter goes to the player with the closest point.

With one point each, the first player can always win a third of the voters, and that is worst-case optimal. The authors study the case where the first player places more than one point and the second places one. They give lower bounds on the first player's guaranteed wins that improve existing bounds for all cases with at least four points. As a by-product they improve bounds on small epsilon-nets for convex ranges, and they also give bounds under a second way of measuring distance.
arxiv-2602-16818:
The HAWC Collaboration probes IceCube neutrino alerts with the HAWC gamma-ray observatory. Neutrino output from space sources is a long-sought sign of cosmic-ray speeding. IceCube has seen a diffuse flux of tera- to peta-electronvolt neutrinos, but very few confirmed sources have emerged. The recent IceCat-1 list names the most promising space neutrino events since May 2011.

Using archived HAWC data, the team runs a coincidence hunt for gamma rays and neutrinos with a Bayesian Block code, covering hundreds of alerts in HAWC's view through July 2025. About five percent show coincident hits, in line with background hopes. Two hits hold the active galaxies Markarian 421 and Markarian 501. The paper weighs how likely the hits are false alarms and surveys the results.
arxiv-2602-17018:
Giovanni Rosa, David Moreno-Lumbreras, and Raula Gaikovina Kula study plugin upkeep for knowledge-centric groups, focusing on Obsidian. Adoption of third-party libraries has become integral to modern software development, leading to large networks such as PyPI, NPM, and Maven, where contributors usually share expertise to sustain extensions. In groups not made up only of developers, maintaining plugins can present different challenges.

Obsidian is a knowledge-centric platform whose users focus on writing, organization, and creativity, yet has built a large plugin set anyway. The paper investigates what kinds of plugins exist in that hybrid set and lays a foundation for understanding how they are maintained. Using repository mining and language-model-based topic modeling on a sample of nearly four hundred plugins, six topics are identified. They cover dynamic editing and organization, interface and layouts, creative writing and productivity, knowledge sync, linking and script tools, and workflow enhancement.
arxiv-2602-17218:
Antonio Capolupo led a four-author team proposing a lab test for a dark matter idea: a hidden neutron partner that mixes weakly with ordinary neutrons. Hidden-sector theories predict such a neutral partner, and the mixing would make neutrons oscillate between visible and dark states. The paper shows that macroscopic quantum interferometry can catch that oscillation directly.

A Mach-Zehnder interferometer fed with very cold neutrons turns the oscillation into phase-dependent intensity patterns. Controlled phase shifts plus tunable magnetic fields and material potentials allow resonant scans of the hidden-sector parameter space. The authors find that existing cold-neutron facilities could probe extremely tiny mixing strengths and mass splittings, opening a previously unexplored region relevant to baryonic dark matter. Neutron interferometry thus becomes a precision tool for hidden-sector physics.
arxiv-2602-17318:
Patrick Zojer led a three-author team testing whether flexible job scheduling pays off in high-performance computing clusters. Traditional rigid scheduling leaves resources idle and jobs waiting, while malleable jobs let the scheduler adjust resource allocations at runtime. Using real workload traces from three supercomputers, the team simulated varying shares of malleable jobs with the ElastiSim software. The study covers five scheduling strategies, including a novel one that holds malleable jobs at their preferred allocation when possible.

Against fully rigid workloads, malleable jobs improved every key metric. With the best strategy per machine, turnaround times, makespans, and wait times all fell sharply, while node utilization rose. Gains stayed substantial even when only a fifth of jobs were malleable. The study links workload traits like runtimes and node needs to malleability shares and strategy choice, encouraging wider adoption of flexible scheduling.
arxiv-2602-17418:
Diana Addae led a six-author team on privacy design for AI apps aimed at children. Kids use AI tools, yet privacy risks for them are rising, and firms find it hard to meet rules that require safeguards. The article proposes a Privacy-by-Design framework that pushes designers to act early and avoid risk.

The framework draws rules from the GDPR in Europe, PIPEDA in Canada, and COPPA in the United States. It then maps them onto each app stage: data collection, model training, live monitoring, and ongoing checks. For each stage it lists practical controls from recent research, so providers can cut privacy risk while meeting legal standards. Child guidance comes from the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and the UK Age-Appropriate Design Code.
arxiv-2602-17518:
Francesca Pezzuti led a five-author team picturing agentic search. With automated systems firing search queries beside humans, retrieval faces a major shift. Yet retrieval stays human-centred: its systems, metrics, user models, and data sets fit human queries and habits. So retrieval runs on assumptions that no longer hold, as workloads and querying habits change.

That mismatch hits performance: caching may lose power, pre-processing may add load without better results, and metrics may misread satisfaction. Without change, models risk pleasing neither side. Yet data sets catching agent search habits are scarce, a grave gap. The team gathers data agentic retrieval-augmented systems produce and use in answering queries, releasing the Agentic Search Queryset data set. It holds thoughts, retrieved documents, and reasoning-induced queries from HotpotQA, Researchy Questions, and MS MARCO, for three agents and two pipelines. A toolkit extends it to new agents, retrievers, and data sets.
arxiv-2602-17618:
Jan Boruch and team introduce a fermionic version of three-dimensional gravity in anti-de Sitter space. They sum over geometries equipped with spin structure, and propose a holographic match to fermionic two-dimensional conformal field theory data. Pure three-dimensional gravity is already thought to admit such a match, and fermions add new structure.

The gravity path integral with one and two torus boundaries yields the spectrum and its statistics from the torus wormhole. Fermionic black hole microstates appear even with no bulk fermionic matter. Subtle topological field theories, sorted by cobordism groups, are folded in. The resulting statistics match anomaly patterns expected from fermionic conformal field theory, and a fermionic random-matrix framework rounds out the match.
arxiv-2602-17718:
Dimitris Vartziotis presents a side-by-side test study of planar curves from a Fourier series whose frequencies are prime numbers. The series, introduced in a companion work, is sampled in the complex plane to yield curves of multi-size geometric tangle. The question is whether that tangle reflects arithmetic structure or merely sparsity or density.

To test it, the prime frequency model is set against random controls: random frequency sets, a Cramér type random model, and a shuffled coefficient model. Using the same box counting rules and Monte Carlo ensembles, prime frequency curves show stable scale-dependent conduct that random models fail to copy. All results are tests, offered as evidence to motivate further theory work rather than as proofs.
arxiv-2602-18218:
I. Ourahou and eleven co-authors report the first hunt for dark photons by the Dandelion experiment. The search targets dark matter particles near one milli-electron-volt, using a spherical mirror to turn them into ordinary millimeter-wave photons. Those photons are caught by an array of 221 kinetic inductance detectors, cooled far below one degree, inside the KISS-NIKA camera.

From nearly twenty-five hours of data, the team battled room-temperature glow and stray light swings, stripping them with a decorrelation method built from detectors outside the expected signal path. The dark photon signal came out consistent with zero. That sets a new cap on how strongly such particles mix with ordinary light, for masses between zero point six and one point four milli-electron-volts. These are the first limits of their kind from a detector array of this type at millimeter wavelengths.
arxiv-2602-18518:
Attila Dobi and four co-authors measure how much violating content users see. Their 2026 paper studies prevalence: the share of views going to violating content on a given day. Safety teams need metrics for what users experience, not only what is reported. Accurate measurement is hard: violations are rare and human labeling is costly.

The team presents a sampling-based measurement system. Daily random samples come from impressions, with ML-assisted weights aiming labels at high-exposure, high-risk content, keeping unbiasedness. Sampled items are labeled by a multimodal LLM with policy prompts and gold-set validation. The system produces prevalence estimates with confidence intervals and drilldowns. One global sample serves many cuts: the same sample supports prevalence by surface, geography, age, and other segments through post-stratified math. The team also describes estimators, variance and interval building, label-quality checks, and a workflow usable across policies.
arxiv-2602-19018:
Neutron stars cool after X-ray superbursts, and that cooling can reveal what lies in their oceans. Hao Huang, with four co-authors, proposes in 2026 an explanation for rapid cooling of the neutron star in MAXI J1752-457 after its superburst. The cause is extra neutrino emission from cycles of electron capture and beta-minus decay. Those cycles involve odd-A nuclei, known as Urca pairs.

That would be the first indication of a nuclear Urca process. Observations by two Japanese satellites imply a hot ignition layer near the Urca shell, with a maximum temperature of about four gigakelvin. The nuclear Urca process then dominates for up to about two days after the superburst. That behaviour differs from normal Type-I bursts, triggered by hydrogen or helium burning in shallower layers. Long-term crust cooling monitoring could thus probe superburst ashes through Urca pairs.
arxiv-2602-19318:
Ngô's proof of the fundamental lemma opened a study of how abelian fibrations break apart under the decomposition theorem. Davesh Maulik and two co-authors write notes describing a framework for dualizable abelian fibrations, the setting where an extra duality structure is present. When that structure exists, the decomposition theorem and the perverse filtration, which layers cohomological information, show especially rich patterns.

The notes lay out the framework and discuss recent progress and applications. Rather than proving one new theorem, the paper organizes ideas that link duality, decomposition, and filtration into a usable picture. Readers get a guided entry to a corner of algebraic geometry where symmetry clarifies structure, and a sense of where current work is heading.
arxiv-2602-19918:
Private inference lets parties run a model without revealing sensitive data, but most protocols assume the data owner follows the rules. A 2026 arXiv paper by Jiaqi Xue and two co-authors shows that assumption fails against a malicious client, and proposes a robust protocol, RobPI, in response.

The authors first design an inference manipulation attack against leading private inference protocols, letting a malicious client shift model outputs with far fewer queries than current black-box attacks need. RobPI counters by weaving encryption-compatible noise into logits and features, bolstering security against such clients. Experiments across networks and data sets show a large drop in attack success and a large rise in the queries attacks require. The work hardens private inference for adversaries who do not play fair.
arxiv-2602-20118:
Testing many hypotheses at once inflates false positives, and Bonferroni's correction, the classic fix, is notorious for low power when tests depend on each other. A 2026 arXiv paper by Caleb Hiltunen and Yeonwoo Rho proposes a practical modification for the case where test statistics are jointly normal and exchangeable.

The method is designed to feel intuitive to practitioners. Simulations suggest it achieves higher power in sparse alternatives, where only a few hypotheses are truly false. The authors also prove the method holds the family-wise error rate below any chosen significance level, so the gain in power does not come at the cost of more false positives. Readers gain a usable Bonferroni variant for dependent, exchangeable normal test statistics.
arxiv-2602-20318:
P. Nedialkov and eight co-authors expand the census of quasars behind the disk of Andromeda, M31. Such background quasars probe the chemical content of M31 gas and anchor proper-motion measurements, but few had reliable redshifts. The team followed up thirty-two quasar candidates with spectroscopy. They confirmed twenty-three quasars, including two new discoveries, and published sixteen spectra for the first time.

The paper reports new uniform redshifts for thirty-four quasars, combining new and archival spectra, and gathers all reliable cases into a total of one hundred twenty-four within a stated brightness boundary. Low-resolution redshifts were compared across sources, and suspect objects were excluded. Reddening estimates show most background quasars suffer little extinction and miss the most obscured regions, reflecting a bias toward brighter, less obscured candidates. Fainter quasars behind nearby galaxies are still needed, and low-resolution redshifts demand caution.
arxiv-2602-20718:
Yangsen Chen and Hao Wang rebuild deformable endoscopic tissue in 3D, a step toward robot-aided surgery. Current 3D Gaussian Splatting methods struggle to give steady tissue surfaces, while NeRF-based methods lack real-time rendering.

Their method, also based on 3D Gaussian Splatting, pursues both smooth soft looks and real-time rendering. It first builds a mesh with a Sign Distance Field method, then uses that mesh to constrain the Splatting rebuild. Local stiffness and global flex limits guide Gaussian shape shifts for highly soft tissue, and tests show solid rebuild quality in both textures and shapes.
arxiv-2602-21218:
Private corpora cannot be shared freely, yet fake data needs to mirror them. Amin Banayeeanzade and eight co-authors propose a light private maker in this 2026 arXiv paper. EPSVec steers language-model making with data-set vectors, paths in firing space catching the gap between private data and public priors. Vectors are pulled and cleaned just once, then standard reading out runs.

Unlinking the privacy budget from making allows at-will many fake samples at no extra privacy cost, with strong trueness even in low-data regimes. Pre-taught base models plus fixed-shot prompting further boost variety and trueness. Trials show better spread match and downstream use than base cases, above all where data is scarce, at far lower compute extra cost.
arxiv-2602-21318:
Chemical graph theory uses degree-based indices to summarize molecular structure, but how those indices relate is not always clear. Duaa Abdullah and Jasem Hamoud clarify the connections among three tree indices in this 2026 arXiv paper: Albertson, Sombor, and Sigma. The Sigma index, measuring quadratic degree deviation, tightly controls the Sombor index through sharp two-sided bounds.

As a direct result, Sombor and Sigma are asymptotically equivalent up to constant factors. A pure theta-relationship between Sombor and Albertson follows from extremal trees with fixed degree sequence, showing quadratic degree interactions and absolute degree disparities scale together there. Sombor emerges as an intermediate descriptor, capturing both global dispersion and local edge irregularity in trees.
arxiv-2602-21418:
Mohammadsaleh Razmi and one co-author present a wearable activity-recognition system that runs inference inside a shank-mounted motion sensor. The goal is low-latency control of a lower-limb exoskeleton. Standard setups stream raw inertial data to a microcontroller for classification, which costs power and time.

Their system instead runs a lightweight decision-tree model on the embedded machine-learning core of an STMicroelectronics LSM6DSV16X sensor. The host microcontroller sleeps and wakes only on an interrupt, reading the recognized label from sensor registers. Tests focus on stance, level walking, and stair ascent. The design cuts computation and radio overhead, saves battery, and sharpens the hard distinction between level walking and stair ascent for torque-assist control.
arxiv-2602-21818:
Guibin Chen leads a team behind SkyReels V4, a unified multi-mode video base model for video-audio work, fill-in, and editing. It uses a dual-stream Diffusion design, one branch making video, the other making synced audio, sharing a text encoder from multi-mode language models. SkyReels V4 accepts multi-mode inputs: text, images, clips, masks, and audio samples.

Multi-mode order use with in-context learning lets the model inject visual guidance under setups, while the audio branch uses cues. A channel joining setup unifies fill-in tasks such as image to video, video stretch, and video editing under one roof, reaching vision-led fill-in via multi-mode prompts. SkyReels V4 supports 1080p detail, 32 frames per second, and 15 second length, for high-quality multi-shot cinema video with synced audio. A speed plan makes low-detail sequences and high-detail frames, plus super-detail frame fills.
arxiv-2602-22118:
Trials cyclists hop, balance, and ride on one wheel with ease that robots rarely match. Benjamin Bokser and forty-one co-authors present the Ultra Mobility Vehicle, a robot that pairs a bicycle with a reaction mass to move with few powered joints. A simulation-driven design search shaped its linkage for jump height and momentum-based balancing on a single wheel contact.

Trained with constrained reinforcement learning, the robot transfers athletic moves to the real machine with no extra tuning: track-stands, jumps, wheelies, rear-wheel hops, and front flips. It runs at brisk speeds and clears obstacles about its own height. The design shows how little actuation a truly agile bicycle robot may need.
arxiv-2602-22418:
How cosmic rays travel through the inner solar system depends on particle drift and the large-scale magnetic field, and radial gradients are the key diagnostic. Zigong Xu and thirteen co-authors use Solar Orbiter's High Energy Telescope, which dives toward the Sun every half year, to measure anomalous cosmic-ray helium in the inner heliosphere. They analyze helium observations in a mid-energy band, excluding solar energetic particle events.

Focusing on quiet times, the team extracts the radial gradient of anomalous helium, advancing understanding of how drift and magnetic structure shape cosmic-ray transport. Solar Orbiter's repeated perihelion passes make such gradients measurable close to the Sun. Space physicists gain a cleaner picture of particle transport where the solar wind is young.
arxiv-2602-22718:
Rui Wei and seven co-authors make reinforcement learning from human feedback cheaper to run. RLHF aligns language models with human taste and sharpens reasoning, but training and inference share the machine, so resource needs swing through the workflow. Server-based frameworks waste capacity in idle gaps between or within components.

RLHFless, the first scalable synchronous RLHF framework on serverless computing, adapts to shifting demands across the pipeline. It pre-computes shared prefixes to dodge repeat work, scales actors with cost in mind given varied response lengths, and balances loads to cut intra-function idle time. On physical testbeds and a large simulated cluster, it ran up to about a third faster and cut costs nearly forty-five percent against the leading baseline.
arxiv-2602-22818:
Remi Cadene and sixteen co-authors unify robot learning in one open-source library. Progress has sped up with cheap teleoperation, large open datasets, and scalable learning methods, yet development stalls on fragmented, closed tools that cover only slices of the robotics stack.

LeRobot spans the whole stack, from low-level middleware for motor control to large-scale dataset collection, storage, and streaming. Built for real-world robots, it supports accessible hardware while staying extensible to new bodies, and it ships efficient versions of leading robot-learning algorithms across paradigms plus a generalized asynchronous inference stack. By favouring scalable learning over hand-crafted pipelines, it lowers entry barriers and gives researchers a reproducible platform.
arxiv-2602-23118:
Sabarnya Mitra and two co-authors analyze universal and non-universal finite-volume effects near the chiral phase transition in two-plus-one flavour QCD. This proceeding presents a finite-size scaling analysis of the order parameter for the chiral transition in QCD with two massless quarks. It uses lattice QCD data with highly improved staggered quarks over a range of light quark masses and several spatial volumes.

Infinite-volume extrapolated data for the order parameter agree reasonably well with expected O(2) scaling behaviour even for physical light-to-strange quark mass ratios. The team quantifies deviations from asymptotic scaling and analyzes finite-size effects in terms of temperature and quark masses at a fixed lattice cutoff. The analysis improves the reliability of the infinite-volume estimate of the chiral order parameter and sharpens the determination of the chiral transition temperature from direct lattice QCD simulations.
arxiv-2602-23318:
Aloïs Rautureau and two co-authors extend GRAVE, a strong Monte-Carlo tree search variant for general game playing, for memory-limited settings. GRAVE's strength comes at a cost: it stores extra win and visit statistics at every node, which makes it impractical where memory is tight and limits its real-world use.

Three new algorithms address the cost in different ways. GRAVE2 uses two-level search, GRAVER recycles nodes, and GRAVER2 combines both techniques. The enhancements drastically cut the number of stored nodes while matching GRAVE's playing strength. For practitioners, the result is a practical route to GRAVE-level play on devices and settings where memory, not compute, is the binding constraint.
arxiv-2602-23418:
Malyali and 13 co-authors present new X-ray, optical, and UV observations of the tidal disruption event candidate J2344. Between 50 and 60 days after peak optical brightness, the source showed large-amplitude modulations in its zero point two to two keV emission. Flux repeatedly dimmed and re-brightened by a factor of about six over a roughly three-day timescale. The modulations showed harder-when-brighter behavior.

The same modulations did not appear in high-cadence observations at 60 to 70 days and 170 to 200 days after peak. The system instead varied stochastically in X-rays over hours-long timescales. The authors discuss the physical mechanisms that could drive such exotic variability and explore one candidate in depth. One candidate is Lense-Thirring precession of the inner accretion flow around the disrupting black hole, which could imprint the observed pattern.
arxiv-2602-23518:
Arkaprabha Ganguli and six co-authors untangle the hidden spaces of deep generative models for dark matter halo maps. Such models compress high-dimensional data but often tangle distinct physical factors together. That hides what each hidden dimension means.

Their framework guides maps of thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich signals with halo mass and concentration as helper variables. A light alignment penalty pushes hidden dimensions to track those physical traits. Extending latent conditional flow matching, their Disentangled Latent-CFM model recovers the known mass-concentration scaling law. It flags hidden-space outliers that may mark unusual halo formation pasts. The hidden space thus becomes a diagnostic tool for cosmic structure, linking coordinates to clear astrophysics.
arxiv-2602-24018:
Andreas Angelou and Marc Moonen propose master-assisted channel estimation for cell-free massive MIMO networks, a key technology for next-generation wireless systems. The 2026 paper considers distributed access points that jointly serve users, where standard models assume no correlation between access-point channels, seemingly removing any benefit from centralized processing.

The authors show that careful pilot design can correlate the signals access points receive during pilot transmission, so centralization can still help. In the proposed scheme, a subset of access points fuse and forward their pilot signals to a master access point, which estimates channels from the fused signals plus its own. That partial centralization balances local and fully centralized processing, improving estimation over purely local methods while cutting fronthaul signaling and compute. Numerical tests confirm consistent gains.
arxiv-2602-24218:
R. Castellanos and ten co-authors report the first spectroscopic identification of the main sequence in Westerlund 1, the most massive known young star cluster in the Milky Way. The 2026 paper tackles a long controversy over the cluster's age, which high foreground extinction had blocked by hiding the main sequence from detection.

Using multi-epoch near-infrared spectroscopy, the team analyzed spectra of about a hundred members with stellar atmosphere models, populating the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram and comparing it with evolutionary isochrones. Observations add dozens of newly identified members with late-O to early-B spectral types. The cluster turn-off gives an age around five and a half million years at a distance near four kiloparsecs. It has moderate coevality, robust to reasonable changes in distance, extinction law, rotation, and metallicity. Infrared data support a single star formation episode, reinforcing Westerlund 1 as a benchmark for massive star evolution.
arxiv-2603-00018: Sebek presents a Newton-based method for finding left eigenvalues of quaternion matrices. Standard real and complex linear-algebra kernels, reached through embeddings, drive it, and it works for matrices of any size. Tests on published cases and benchmark sets, plus a compact MATLAB reference code, show checkable certificate-based runs up to size 64 by 64. It also spots multiple spherical parts and odd cases such as extra lone left eigenvalues and left-spectrum deficiency.
arxiv-2603-00218: Zhu and colleagues present GLIDE-Reg, a global-to-local deformable registration system that tunes a registration field together with a learnable dimensionality reduction module, fusing global semantic cues with MIND local descriptors. It scores the highest Dice coefficients across six anatomical structures in Lung250M, NLST and UCLA5DCT cohorts, beating DEEDS in all three. Target registration errors reach 1.58 mm on Lung250M landmarks, between corrField and DEEDS, and match DEEDS on NLST nodule centres, showing robustness for nodule tracking.
arxiv-2603-00318: Wang presents the Agent Economic Sovereignty Protocol, a layered design letting AI agents transact on their own at machine speed while staying bound to human-set limits by cryptography. The protocol enforces one rule: agents may move money but never control it outright. It combines an eight-check policy engine, tiered human review, dual-signed escrow deals, context-isolated privacy, and a cryptographic base. Wang sets out a pair of testable hypotheses on security coverage and latency cost, and specifies a full evaluation method with baselines and ablations.
arxiv-2603-00418: Kim, Seo, and Kim fuse sparse weather station readings with satellite images to paint rainfall fields where radar cover is thin or costly. Their query conditioned splatting renders only queried rainy spots instead of the whole image plane, saving work while keeping sharp rain edges. A proposal net spots likely rain points, and a neural field predicts splat traits for each. Benchmark tests beat gridded products by over half on error, holding strong across varied space and time scales.
arxiv-2603-00618: Sun and six colleagues rethink multi domain graph pretraining through Riemannian geometry, asking how knowledge actually moves and merges across domains. Their key idea merges any graph data set into one smooth curved space, described locally by an adaptive orthogonal frame and then glued into a coherent whole. The resulting GraphGlue system supports batched pretraining with EMA prototyping and offers a transfer score based on geometric consistency. Tests show it leads across diverse graph domains.
arxiv-2603-00918: Kim and Cho introduce SOLACE, a post-training method that rewards text-to-image models using their own self-confidence instead of outside judges. The model re-noises its own images and earns higher reward when it recovers the injected noise well, turning that signal into reinforcement-learning rewards without annotators or preference data. The approach improves composition, text rendering, and image-text alignment, and pairs well with external rewards while easing reward hacking.
arxiv-2603-01718:
Yossi Ben-Zion, Eden Cohen, and Nitza Davidovitch track how journal articles changed after AI writing tools spread in late 2022. Their 2026 study reads the full run of a large open journal across seven years. More than one hundred thousand articles let them watch length, team size, and cross-border teamwork at population scale.

Manuscripts grew longer in all groups, with the largest gains for authors based in Africa and Asia. That growth cut the word-count gap with native English-speaking authors by a large share. Non-native English authors also shrank their teams and co-wrote far less with native English partners. Native English groups held steady on both teamwork measures, while reference counts rose mildly for all. The pattern hints that new tools reshape not just prose, but who writes together.
arxiv-2603-01818:
Hang Yu, Liao Sun, Shaokun Liu, and colleagues watch an atomic resonance change shape as space squeezes from three dimensions toward two. Their 2026 lab work uses an ultracold lithium Fermi gas held in a one-dimensional optical lattice. A Feshbach resonance lets atomic interactions spike at a set magnetic field.

In the three-dimensional limit, atom loss near the resonance leans on one orbital channel with twofold symmetry. As lattice confinement grows, the balance between the two orbital channels shifts in a smooth way. The favored channel fades, which the team traces to orbital-dependent changes in the p-wave interactions. Branching ratios and resonance shifts both support that reading of the data. The work shows confinement as a knob for orbital control in strongly interacting quantum gases.
arxiv-2603-02218:
Wei Liu, Siya Qi, Yali Du, and Yulan He ask when self-play can keep improving a language model in this 2026 paper. In self-play, a model makes tasks, tries them, and learns from the results. Many such loops stall fast, the authors note. The data they make adds volume but no new learnable content.

Experiments on a coding task pin down what a working loop needs. New data must carry more learnable content in each round than the last. The model plays three roles: proposer, solver, and checker of answers. Three design fixes target growth in learnable content from those roles. Roles can evolve in a loop, budgets can grow with content, and fresh outside tasks can prevent stalls.
arxiv-2603-02818:
Hikaru Wakaura cuts the cost of a quantum neural network design by packing more data into each circuit run. The 2026 paper concerns Chebyshev quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, where each edge function is evaluated as a quantum inner product. That design trades qubit count against the number of circuit runs per pass.

Merged amplitude encoding loads the combined input-edge products for one output node into a single quantum state, cutting runs by a factor equal to the input count. The price is only one or two extra qubits, and the computed value stays exactly the same. Across ten network setups and sixteen random seeds, tests under ideal, sampled, and noisy simulation showed no meaningful loss in trainability. Digit sorting scores also matched the original design.
arxiv-2603-02918:
David Ortiz del Campo, Tobias Galla, and Raúl Toral study a follower system that syncs with its driver's future. Anticipated synchronization sounds impossible, yet a driven system can lock onto what the driver will do next when the coupling carries a delay. Prior work assumed one single delay time.

Real couplings spread delays over a range, so the authors extend the theory to distributed delay times. Their main result shows approximate anticipation can hold across a band of coupling strengths for a given delay spread. For linear oscillators they find simple cases with exact sync, up to a scale factor. Simulations of chaotic systems confirm stable approximate anticipation. The work widens a curious effect toward the messy delays of real networks.
arxiv-2603-03018:
Yuvraj Agrawal designs an architecture that keeps AI agents honest when they query company engineering data. Firms log huge, messy streams from code hosts, build pipelines, trackers, and monitoring tools. Language models could automate over that telemetry, but raw streams overflow context and local metric definitions keep shifting.

His system, REGAL, treats exact deterministic computation as the base layer, and lets models act only through a bounded, versioned tool set. A layered data pipeline produces replayable, compressed gold-standard artifacts. A registry then compiles declared metric definitions into matching tools, so specification and execution cannot drift apart. A prototype case study shows the approach is feasible and helps with speed, token cost, and governance.
arxiv-2603-03118:
A. R. Knyazev, A. Lachmann, A. G. Goodman, and colleagues ask whether waves inside a stellarator can knock its fastest ions out of orbit. Stellarators confine fusion plasma with twisted magnetic fields, and shear Alfvén waves ripple through that field. Their 2026 paper studies optimized designs that otherwise hold energetic particles well.

A semi-analytical resonance model, extended to all the symmetric design families, predicts where wave and particle motion lock together. Adding more field periods calmed the chaos in two families but not the third. Wave-driven jumps between passing and trapped orbits caused real losses in two families, while the quasi-isodynamic design resisted. The team computed the wave sizes that trigger prompt loss of fusion-born alpha particles at power-plant scale.
arxiv-2603-03218:
Aditya Kumar Purohit, Yuwei Liu, Manon Berney, and colleagues audit the McDonald's self-ordering kiosk for manipulative design. Kiosks speed ordering and raise average spend, but their flows can also steer customers through dark patterns, interface tricks that pressure or mislead. Their 2026 study applies a temporal framework that tracks patterns across the whole interaction.

Walking through a time-pressured order in Germany, they reconstructed twelve steps and cataloged the tactics at three levels. Strategies included adding steps, false hierarchy, bad defaults, hidden information, and pressured selling, down to small tricks like confirmshaming and split pricing. Patterns accumulate along the linear kiosk flow and gain force from the physical setting. The authors argue such hybrid interfaces deserve regulatory attention.
arxiv-2603-03318:
Nikita Kuznetsov, Niyaz Ismagilov, and Ernesto Campos bring a quantum-inspired twist to the attention mechanism inside language models. Attention lets a transformer weigh how tokens relate, but it grows costly as models scale. Quantum natural language processing has offered its own attention designs, tested mostly on simple classification. Their 2026 paper moves the idea into full text generation for the first time.

The team builds a classical quantum-inspired self-attention block and installs it in GPT-1's complete autoregressive pipeline. Against standard attention, their version cuts character errors, word errors, and prediction loss by large multiples. The cost is inference that takes a few times longer. The trade-off frames a fresh direction for cheaper, sharper language modeling.
arxiv-2603-03418:
Yimin Zhu and eight colleagues adapt a new connection scheme to classify hyperspectral images. Such images record many narrow color bands per pixel and feed maps for environmental and resource work. Their mixed spatial and spectral patterns are hard to learn from and harder to explain. Their 2026 model combines the Mamba sequence architecture with DeepSeek's manifold-constrained hyper-connections, a recent upgrade to standard residual links.

A clustering-guided module learns spatial and spectral features together inside that framework. The connection weights double as soft cluster membership maps, which makes the model's grouping of the scene readable. Spectral bands are also split into physically meaningful groups that run as parallel streams, tying the design to real optics. Benchmark tests show better accuracy than leading rivals, with the added benefit that the model's decisions are easier to interpret.
arxiv-2603-03618:
Juampablo E Heras Rivera and seven colleagues assemble a benchmark that types brain tumors the way clinicians must, from incomplete evidence. Real diagnosis merges brain MRI, microscope slides of stained tissue, and written pathology reports, and some pieces are often missing. Their 2026 dataset, CoRe-BT, covers three hundred ten patients, all with multi-sequence MRI, and ninety-five with paired tissue images and reports as well.

Every case carries a tumor type and grade across six clinically relevant classes, mostly glioma subtypes, and the MRI volumes include expert-drawn tumor masks. The benchmark varies which modalities are available and compares MRI-only models against fusion models that add pathology when present. Baselines prove fusion feasible and show each modality contributing something the others lack. The authors offer CoRe-BT as a grounded testbed for robust multimodal learning.
arxiv-2603-03718:
Risto Ojala, Tristan Ellison, and Mo Chen teach a vision system to see the invisible: glass. Transparent surfaces carry almost no visual signature of their own, yet robots and scene understanding must treat them as solid. Their 2026 architecture attacks the problem with two backbones at once, one supplying general visual features, the other task-trained features specific to glass.

The general features come from a frozen DINOv3 foundation model, the learned ones from a supervised Swin transformer. Their multi-scale outputs are compressed by a residual channel-reduction stage and decoded into masks by a Mask2Former head. On four standard glass segmentation datasets the system sets state-of-the-art marks on several accuracy metrics. Its inference speed rivals the previous champion, and beats it outright with a lighter backbone variant. Code and trained weights are public.
arxiv-2603-03818:
Huihan Liu and four colleagues find that big pretrained robot brains forget far less than small ones trained from nothing. Continual learning, adding skills without erasing old ones, is a classic robot headache, studied mostly in small imitation policies. Their 2026 paper tests modern pretrained vision-language-action models and finds the dynamics transformed: the pretrained models are remarkably resistant to catastrophic forgetting.

Plain experience replay, the simplest remedy, works startlingly well on them, sometimes producing zero forgetting with only a small replay buffer. Pretraining itself deserves the credit, pairing low forgetting with strong learning of the new skill. Even when performance on an old task dips mid-training, the knowledge is not gone: brief fine-tuning recovers the seemingly lost skill rapidly. Scale, the authors conclude, changes continual learning from damage control into accumulation.
arxiv-2603-04018: Pautasso and Ronchi Della Rocca revisit principal typing for intersection types, forty-five years later. A type assignment system has the principal typing property when every typable term has a special typing yielding all typings. The authors spot three operations, substitution, expansion, and erasure, building any derivation in a head-normalization system. They then design an inference semi-method for principal typings of strongly normalizing terms, a perspective on results proven over forty years ago.
arxiv-2603-04118: Yue and others model and control a pneumatic soft catheter with neural Koopman operators. Robotic catheters promise improved sharpness over manual methods, yet soft catheter models and control remains challenging. The Koopman operator lifts data into a linear space for predictive control, but manual basis functions oversimplify conduct. Their neural method jointly learns the lifted picture and operator. Motivated by cutting fluoroscopy radiation during ablation, they study open-loop control reaching targets without steady feedback. Average errors reach about two millimeters and five degrees, beating rivals.
arxiv-2603-04218: Archer and Laudone study arrow pattern avoidance in permutations, on structure and enumeration. Motivated by these results, the authors initiate a full study of arrow avoidance, proving basic results including arrow-Wilf equivalence, and listing several arrow avoidance classes. Finally, they consider avoidance of arrow-pattern pairs, focusing on cases that forbid fixed points in the core permutation.
arxiv-2603-04518: Jerome Guere proves a Hodge link for rational smooth cubic fourfolds. Prior work by Katzarkov, Kontsevich, Pantev, and Yu studied irrationality of very general complex cubic fourfolds. Guere shows every rational smooth complex cubic fourfold has primitive cohomology isomorphic as a Hodge structure to another cohomology. That target is the twisted middle cohomology of a K3 surface that is projective. The result ties rationality of cubic fourfolds to K3 geometry in a precise way. It thus gives a sharp test for rational fourfolds.
arxiv-2603-04718: Zhang and colleagues simulate justice-specific queries for moot courts. Judges probe attorneys on records and claims. Law schools and attorneys use moot courts to prepare. Using Supreme Court transcripts, the paper asks whether AI can simulate justice-specific queries. Evaluation is hard: no correct question exists per turn, and good queries spot issues and flaws and keep an adversarial tone. A framework assesses realism and usefulness. Both prompt-based and agentic simulators are evaluated. Simulated questions often appear realistic with high recall, yet models show low diversity and sycophancy.
arxiv-2603-05018: Shane Farnsworth and colleagues compare the theory of causal fermion systems against generalized trace dynamics and non-commutative geometry. The three theories differ widely, yet they agree that the geometric structure recovered in the continuum limit is not bare spacetime but a suitable fiber bundle. The key innovation in causal fermion systems, the comparison concludes, lies in how relations between distinct spacetime points are encoded. Where Synge's world function encodes geodesic distance between points, a generalized two-point correlator takes its role, an idea transferring to the other two theories.
arxiv-2603-05318: Christos Fragkathoulas and team present GALACTIC for local and global counterfactuals of unsupervised time-series grouping. Feature-attribution or metadata methods fail to spot shifts across cluster boundaries, while counterfactual accounts have mostly stayed supervised. At instance level, it makes shifts via a cluster-aware objective. At cluster level, typical picking mitigates mind load via an MDL summary of global accounts. Its MDL objective is supermodular, letting a greedy algorithm with provable guarantees. UCR Archive tests show sparser local ones and more concise global summaries.
arxiv-2603-05918: Luo and team analyze ill-posedness in CSI-driven inverse scattering for ISAC matter rebuild. Background-related columns prove highly lined up and rule near rank gap, while scatter-related columns match weakly. Shrinking the region of focus around the true scatter for sure reduces the illness number and tightens the Cramér-Rao bound. An ROI-limited square coding frame follows, with linear sampling marking a coarse region and updates in the reduced sub-space. Full-wave models back state gain, cost savings, and toughness over the full form.
arxiv-2603-06318: Banerjee and his team present new resummed predictions for vector boson pair production at the LHC. Threshold resummation reaches next to next to leading log level and matches next to next to leading order QCD. Resummation cuts scale uncertainties in the results from unphysical renormalization and factorization scales. The resummed corrections lift fixed order results by a few percent for ZZ and WW production.
arxiv-2603-06518: Maki and Hofmann examine tomographic transport in liquids under a magnetic field, where odd-parity Fermi surface bends decay slower than even-parity ones. Without a field, flow shows two such modes; at a critical field, one dies, with the rest set by Landau parameters and growing fluid-dominated at high fields. They use an exact solution of the Boltzmann equation in a calm time approximation for odd- and even-parity modes. A trial approach for deformation backs the analysis, showing angular structure and field strength.
arxiv-2603-06618: Deng and team propose a framework for zero-shot interaction prediction in multiplex biological networks, where multiple link types matter for complex biological systems. Their approach uses foundation models for embeddings and a topology-aware graph splitter catching layers and connectivity. Paired learning aligns codes across modalities, and teacher-student teaching enables zero-shot reach. Tests demonstrate it beats state-of-the-art methods in layered living network link guessing, providing a tool for mapping living links and pushing therapeutics.
arxiv-2603-06818: Bandyopadhyay presents a XOR gate built from a single straintronic magnetic tunnel junction. Standard XOR gates demand conditional dynamics that require multiple switches or gate types, giving large footprints and low logic density. His single junction design cuts footprint and is non-volatile, suiting non-von-Neumann and processor-in-memory designs. Switching is fast and energy per operation is tiny, an order of magnitude below all-transistor XOR designs. Cascading uses a CMOS device for gain, restoration, fan-out, and isolation, which plays no role in gate dynamics.
arxiv-2603-06918: Quang-Anh N. D. and colleagues introduce T2Nav, a zero-shot visual navigation system joining mixed data with graph thinking. Real-world navigation is hard, since systems must adapt to unseen cases, while older learning needs large data and constant tweaks. Foundation models attempt new tasks without extra training, yet many methods accept narrow inputs and underuse details and structure. T2Nav puts visual data into a graph and matches it to the scene, using topology-aware time graph memory and loop finding to strike a balance.
arxiv-2603-07018: Parikh and colleagues present TEA-Time, a system for moving effects across time. Effects from a trial are local to the group and time. Moving findings to groups is well studied, but moving them across time is less studied, and the target is hard. They define the average effect under a time rule, with ID plans, replicated trials and common arm, and build tools for each. In tests, the common arm plan is precise but biased when the time factor tracks the gap between treatment and measure, not measure time.
arxiv-2603-07218: Enabe and colleagues fix a stabilization flaw in low-order virtual element methods for hyperelasticity. Practice integrates a nonlinear surrogate energy over an auxiliary sub-triangulation. Scaled by modified Lame parameters and incompressibility factors, it can make results depend on an arbitrary internal mesh. It can also stiffen shear-type kernel modes in the nearly incompressible regime. Their submesh-free, kernel-only stabilization decouples deviatoric and volumetric channels and scales like the current Newton tangent energy on the kernel. The shear term is scaled solely by a shear measure.
arxiv-2603-07618: Yuan, Androwis and Zhou train device help in stages mirroring how users adjust to a device. Their SMAT plan first teaches unaided gait, then adjusting to device mass, then device help against a steady human policy, and finally joint tuning with full torque and feedback. Tests with a 26-muscle leg model cut hip muscle effort versus no assistance. Offline gait checks and treadmill tests on five subjects confirm steady, mostly positive power delivery.
arxiv-2603-07718: Zhao and colleagues present optical spectra of the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS across several post-perihelion epochs. Post-perihelion production rates cover CN, C3, C2, CH and gaseous iron and nickel. The coma proves less depleted in C2 after perihelion, suggesting buried stirring or mixed makeup. CN and metal rates fall more slowly outbound than inbound, matching reported water behavior, while metals track a CO-bearing reservoir rather than water.
arxiv-2603-07918: Zhang and colleagues sharpen low-resolution hyperspectral images with help from an unregistered sharper image. Their design first applies singular value decomposition for spectral unmixing, keeping the endmembers intact while the network lifts the initial abundance map. A coarse-to-fine deformable aggregation module then borrows spatial texture from it, gauging flow and similarity before fine tuning aligns them. Abundance cross-attention blocks refine the merged output, and a modulated fusion module combines encoder-decoder output through dynamic gating weights.
arxiv-2603-08118: Qiao and colleagues improve model-based offline reinforcement learning, where a learned dynamics model helps explore policies without fresh environment data. Model errors can invite model exploitation, in which the policy leans on flaws in the model and performance degrades. Adversarial model learning counters this with a maximin formulation, and RAMBO is its best-known practical method. Yet the authors find severe Q-value underestimation in RAMBO's implementation. They answer with robust value-aware model learning plus implicitly differentiable adaptive weighting, tying model updates to value accuracy.
arxiv-2603-08318: Dixon and colleagues compare arc and chicane bunch compression schemes for hard and soft X-ray free-electron laser facilities. Such facilities progressively squeeze electron bunches as they accelerate from an injector to the undulators, reaching peak currents needed for efficient lasing without harming transverse brightness. Current ones achieve high peak currents through four-dipole bunch chicanes, but those systems allow projected emittance dilution at the percent level and amplify microbunching. The authors introduce full arc compression and compare it with the standard chicane and a five-dipole variant.
arxiv-2603-08618: Michele Arzano and colleagues test how warped symmetry twists local spin readings on entangled pairs. With a quantum-group symmetry, the usual one-particle action stays, yet the deformed singlet picks a twisted form. Plain tensor-factor readings then show a deformation-tied skew, while braided readings, dressed with the R-matrix, give the opposite skew on the same state.
arxiv-2603-08718: Zhengyuan Shi and colleagues build CktEvo, a benchmark for evolving chip code at repository scale. Chip power, performance, and area emerge from many files plus the toolchain, yet past tests use lone snippets. Their task asks for edits that keep behavior while improving those three measures, with a closed loop tying model edits to toolchain feedback and no human in the loop.
arxiv-2603-08818: Tianyi Li and Jin Wei-Kocsis reflect on breaking into human-computer interaction and aging research from outside. They describe a gap between what aging populations need and what new technologies offer. Volunteering in a senior living community built their empathy for older adults, and the manuscript shares those reflective lessons for interdisciplinary newcomers.
arxiv-2603-08918: Anton Lüders and colleagues prove when a noise-cleaning trick for Brownian walks is exact. The method splits paths into free motion plus interaction shifts, dropping cross terms without prior proof. In thermal equilibrium the cross terms vanish, since velocity links track negative force links exactly, while out of equilibrium they survive as a mark of nonequilibrium physics.
arxiv-2603-09018: Yixiong Chen and colleagues bring medical agent capability offline in a lightweight 4B model. Frontier agents cost too much, run slowly, and risk privacy under API deployment, clashing with on-premise clinical needs. Their Meissa learns when to engage outside help and how to run multi-step interaction from distilled trajectories, matching or beating frontier agents in 10 of 16 settings with fewer parameters.
arxiv-2603-09118: Xueshi Li and colleagues report single photons with shaped wavefronts from quantum dots inside metacavities that use geometric phase. Cavity work usually forces a trade-off between Purcell gain and wavefront control, since each wants an unlike resonator. Their thin monolithic devices, only 200 nm thick, give both effects at once, plus vortex beams and holographic patterns. A lattice of meta-atoms confines light tightly while varied tilts shape what leaves.
arxiv-2603-09218: Chenhui Zuo and colleagues build a simulation framework for designing robots that physically interact with people, from wearables to collaborative humanoids. Real trials cannot easily measure inner states like joint loads or muscle forces. At the core sits a full-body musculoskeletal model, driven by a reinforcement learning controller, acting as a stand-in for human dynamics. A pre-trained motion policy then serves as a steady evaluator, making wide design searches and joint tuning of structure and control tractable.
arxiv-2603-09718: Zhiye Tang and coauthors build GSStream, a system for streaming volumetric scenes built from 3D Gaussian splatting over limited networks. One part forecasts where each viewer will look next, learning from the viewing paths of many users. A second part, trained by reinforcement learning, picks stream quality as network states change. Tests show better picture quality and leaner network use than rival systems.
arxiv-2603-10218: Aquino-López, Muschitiello and Osman bring out BSync, a Bayesian tool for aligning paleoclimate proxy records to set chronologies. Proxy series sit on depth or rough age scales that must map onto calendar time, and old tools return one alignment with little sense of doubt. BSync treats the monotone time map as inference, with a link that locally stretches and squeezes the input scale. Readable rate terms let priors encode how sediment builds up.
arxiv-2603-10318: Ryan J Y Lim and Michael C H Choi study how to pick a two-block split that helps a finite Markov chain mix faster under group averaging. They link two goals, KL divergence and Frobenius distance to stationarity, to the induced projection chain. The first link gives decay rates through the log-Sobolev constant, while the second yields a Cheeger-type cut criterion. Since exact search is costly, they offer practical approximations, and numerical tests show the best cuts cut total variation distance to stationarity a lot.
arxiv-2603-10418: Yijie Li and co-authors present TractoRC, a single system that aligns brain tract scans and groups their streamlines together, two jobs usually done apart. Both jobs seek the same white matter structure, so the team let them share one learned space for streamline points. In that space, alignment uses learned landmark points, while grouping forms bundles from shared patterns. A self-supervised trick keeps the learned features aware of shape even when scans are moved or turned. Doing both jobs together beat leading separate methods on each task.
arxiv-2603-10618: Tatjana Kleine and co-authors show that orbital angular momentum entanglement hides a topology that survives noisy channels, even as the entanglement itself decays. Using atmospheric turbulence as a test case for a stochastic medium, they tracked a topological observable through channels of varied strength. It stayed preserved while the OAM itself proved highly sensitive to the turbulence. The same held for mixed states, with topology intact as purity fell. The authors offer this as a new angle on protecting OAM entanglement, extendable to other bases and channels.
arxiv-2603-10818: M Abumusabh and the Belle and Belle II collaborations report the first searches for lepton-flavor violation with charge, in decays of chi_bJ(1P) bottomonium states. The data hold well over a hundred million Upsilon(2S) decays, collected with the Belle detector at the KEKB collider. The team looked for decays into pairs of charged leptons with mismatched flavors, for J values zero, one, and two. No significant signal appeared. Upper limits on the branching fractions land near one part in a million for electron-muon pairs.
arxiv-2603-11118: Eliran Sherzer builds a learning-based operator that merges non-renewal arrival streams into a single aggregate stream. Old routes use renewal stand-ins, pay heavily for Markovian representations, or track only mean performance. His model is trained on synthetic Markovian arrival processes, where superposition is known. It maps low-order moments and autocorrelation descriptors of the input streams to those of the merge. It beats renewal approximations in varied regimes. In such modules, it enables decomposition-based evaluation of feed-forward queueing networks.
arxiv-2603-11218: Xerxes Arsiwalla and Fernando Olivie Méndez Méndez ask which pre-Lie structures a Lie algebra can carry. They form the Lie-admissible algebras, whose commutator still satisfies the Jacobi identity despite being nonassociative. Two of the five classes are known to exclude semisimple algebras over the complex numbers. The authors work through the other classes, giving the tests for anti-flexible algebras. One example, for the rank-one special linear algebra, is given in full. They prove the last class universal for all such algebras.
arxiv-2603-12218: Khanna, Srivastava, Jain, and Balasubramanian build UniMotion, a gesture recognizer that crosses devices and user groups. IMU gesture tools often fit one device or one population and fail elsewhere. UniMotion pretrains a motion model on plentiful unlabeled activity data in a first stage. A token-based scheme teaches it to spot key motion signatures in time series data. A text-guided classifier then fine-tunes on a small labeled set. Hand and earbud gestures from blind and sighted users both reached strong accuracy with little labeled data.
arxiv-2603-12418: Hoffmann and Meinel pin down the binding energy of the Tbb tetraquark with lattice QCD. Two heavy-quark treatments face a direct test on equal footing in their study. A relativistic anisotropic-clover action, tuned nonperturbatively, drives the new data runs. Older data with a lattice-NRQCD action are reanalyzed with otherwise identical parameters. Combined chiral and continuum extrapolations across seven ensembles give the relativistic result. Both actions land near the same binding energy, lower than an earlier analysis found, a shift traced to correlation matrix choices.
arxiv-2603-12718: Jonathan Bourne and co-authors argue that layout analysis models for documents are scored with the wrong metric. IoU-based F1 was built for images of 3D scenes, not flat printed pages. They show F1 can collapse despite perfect text extraction and can hide parsing errors. Their fix pairs semantic units with MOTe, an error split into missing, overlap, trespass, and excess parts. MOTe tracks character error rates far better than F1. It also picks the lower-error model most of the time.
arxiv-2603-13018: Alexander Gheorghiu asks what support means in one fixed atomic base under Sandqvist's base-extension semantics. The global completeness theorem says which formulae are valid in every base. The local question is what support in a single base amounts to. He shows it coincides with proof-search inside a logic program of second-order hereditary Harrop type. Formulae are encoded as program goals in continuation-passing style. Quantifiers over base extensions act as fresh eigenvariables, not ranges over a totality. Support is thus proof-search, fully constructive in form.
arxiv-2603-13118: Sidaty El Hadramy and co-authors treat medical imaging tasks as mappings learned between continuous function spaces. Most deep tools work on fixed pixel or voxel grids, which ties them to one resolution. NOIR embeds medical signals into shared implicit neural representations. A neural operator then maps between their latent modulations, free of any grid. Tasks from segmentation to synthesis ran on public and in-house datasets. Scores held at native resolution, and results stayed strong on unseen discretizations.
arxiv-2603-13218: Samuel H. Kramer and co-authors compare three cross-correlation methods for line intensity mapping. The method maps the universe by scanning redshifted spectral lines from atoms and molecules. Many target lines are still undetected, and foregrounds plus noise block the signal. The team tests stacking, the conditional voxel intensity distribution, and the cross power spectrum. On simulated EXCLAIM maps, all three detect the [CII] line at high redshifts. Lower noise in a future case sharpens detections and constraints a great deal.
arxiv-2603-13318: Quan Liu and co-authors study why fine-tuning on safety data can cause false refusals in LLMs. Safety sets pair unsafe prompts with stock refusal text, and their token entropy is low. The team builds FlowLens, a PCA-based tool, to map residual-stream geometry in the model. More safety data concentrates variance on a few components, which cuts smoothness and raises false refusals. Their Variance Concentration Loss penalizes that crowding in mid-layer residuals. It cut false refusals by over 35 points while keeping benchmark scores steady.
arxiv-2603-13618: R. M. Strässle, S. A. Hosseini, and I. V. Karlin present local kinetic sensors for adaptive mesh and algorithm refinement. Refinement criteria based on macroscopic variables can be made purely local, which aids scaling. Kinetic models like lattice Boltzmann methods add access to the one-particle distribution function, a richer source. Their new sensors use that access to tailor criteria for compressible, turbulent, and non-equilibrium flows. Validation is followed by a showcase on a discrete velocity Boltzmann solver. The sensors give an accurate, efficient, and scalable path.
arxiv-2603-14218: Hu and Simchi-Levi give a lean way to estimate the excess risk of a trained predictor with only black-box access. Their method needs one dataset and no held-out validation data. It builds pseudo-responses by flipping residual signs at random. Each round then draws two small sub-datasets and refits the model on each. Those refits are far cheaper than full retraining. The authors prove high-probability risk bounds for fixed and random designs, given a well-set noise scale.
arxiv-2603-14318: Sapatnekar surveys electromigration analysis for integrated circuits in this invited paper. Electromigration wears down chip wiring under high current and limits device lifetime. Rule-based checks dominate practice but have known blind spots. Physics-based models give faster, more accurate checks in research, yet industry has not adopted them. The paper contrasts physics models with empirical ones. It closes with open problems that block circuit-aware, physics-based checks in future mixed-chip systems.
arxiv-2603-14418: Yan and co-authors present HierEM, a method for prostate lesion segmentation that learns from uneven hospital labels. Each site contours lesions by its own protocol, so networks overfit local styles and fail at new sites. HierEM treats each label set as a noisy view of one hidden clean mask. An EM loop swaps between guessing that mask and training a network on it as a soft target. Site-level sensitivity and specificity are estimated under a prior. Tests on three cohorts beat top rivals on cross-site reach.
arxiv-2603-14818: Li, Song and Li certify that compressed neural networks behave like their full-size originals with SimCert. Quantization and pruning squeeze networks for embedded hardware. Safety-critical flows must prove the squeeze changed little. Worst-case checks scale poorly and crack on pruned shapes. SimCert gives probabilistic certificates with tunable confidence levels instead. Dual-network symbolic propagation handles both squeeze types. Bernstein bounds sharpen the safety margins. ACAS Xu and vision benchmarks show wins over prior baselines, they report.
arxiv-2603-15018: Sasmal and co-authors give a scalable way to self-test high-dimensional entanglement without trusting the devices. Their scheme certifies a maximally entangled two-qudit state plus a set of mutually anticommuting observables on one side. It rests on a Bell inequality with two separated observers and many settings. A sum-of-squares method yields the best quantum bound with no assumed dimension. They also bound how fidelity drops when the observed Bell value falls short of the ideal.
arxiv-2603-15118: Barzelay and co-authors introduce VAREX, a benchmark for pulling structured data out of government forms. A reverse annotation pipeline fills PDF templates with synthetic values, giving exact ground truth. The set holds 1,777 documents with 1,771 distinct schemas.
