Each document comes as plain text, layout-preserving text, an image, or both. The team tested 20 models, with a focus on small ones under four billion parameters. Below that size, broken output format, not extraction skill, was the main bottleneck. Fine-tuning a small model fixed much of the gap.
arxiv-2603-15418: Shaik and co-authors replace the learned central critic in multi-agent reinforcement learning with a fine-tuned vision-language model. Training a critic from scratch wastes samples and generalizes poorly. Their critic reads a task description in words, visual paths of the agents, and structured state data. This removes critic learning from policy training, which boosts sample efficiency. The resulting policies stay small enough for weak robots. Tests show sound zero-shot return estimates across model backbones, on both familiar and new scenarios.
arxiv-2603-15518: Liu and co-authors diagnose why same-subject knowledge edits in large language models fail to generalize to new phrasings. Edited facts recall fine in their original form but vanish under fresh instructions. They trace the collapse to activation drift from prompt changes that exceeds the model's post-edit tolerance. Joint training with orthogonal gradients lands in sharp minima, and the covariance rule amplifies input wobble. Their RoSE method aligns representations isotropically and layers knowledge in stages. Tests show much stronger instruction following after edits.
arxiv-2603-15718: Prodinger extends a recent study of Fibonacci numbers along residue classes. The sequence F at steps dn+h was covered before only for h equal to zero. The general h case proves more involved. Chebyshev polynomials supply the main tool for the harder case. Convolutions of the sequence fall under the same treatment. The short note builds directly on the earlier arXiv study. It completes the picture for all residue shifts h.
arxiv-2603-15818: Bekhouche and co-authors build a detector for ambivalence and hesitancy in people. Such states show as clashes between words, voice, and face. Text-only tools over-flag the state and miss its absence. Their ConflictAwareAH model reads video, audio, and text feeds. Pairwise gaps between modality embeddings act as two-way cues. Big gaps flag conflict, small gaps confirm calm consistency. A text-guided late fusion step adds further gains. The model hit 0.694 Macro F1 on the BAH test split. Training took under 25 minutes on one GPU.
arxiv-2603-16118: Shin and co-authors track robot motion with poses carried whole on the SE(3) manifold. IMU propagation feeds fast motion guesses between LiDAR sweeps. Older methods split rotation and translation onto separate paths. Rotation change then leaks poorly into position updates. Their joint pose form folds spin into travel directly. Correlated pose errors shape the warp fix for scans. That uncertainty joins the measurement noise in compensation. Diverse datasets validate the SE(3)-LIO system end to end. Code and extra material ship with the study.
arxiv-2603-16218: Hechtl and co-authors add velocity signals to vision-language-action robot policies. Standard cloning methods output poses at low rates, with no velocity feedforward. That forces stiff control, which hurts safe contact. Two fixes are offered. One estimates velocity by finite differences, and works with current models. The other uses cubic B-spline actions for smooth, continuous paths. Tests on a cube-in-hole task showed faster work from the first fix. The spline fix kept success rates high.
arxiv-2603-16318: Manolescu and Mohanarangan study FK-percolation as its transition nears the borderline case q = 4. Past q = 4, the transition turns discontinuous. They hold the model at its critical point and let q sink toward 4. In that limit, the correlation length becomes isotropic, the same in all directions. The proof leans on rotational invariance results at q = 4. The Wulff crystal of the model grows round in step.
arxiv-2603-16418: Muller and co-authors find quantum limits for measuring surface roughness. Roughness matters across engineering and precision manufacturing. They use passive linear optics with quantum estimation methods. The team derives top precision bounds for spatial moments of point sources. Sources sit below the diffraction scale in three dimensions. For the height profile, moment information is capped by a constant. A mode-sorting imaging method reaches the bound for roughness. Classical imaging cannot.
arxiv-2603-16818: Chu and co-authors explore using large language models to mine cloud incident reports. Vendors publish these reports after failures, but the text is long and unstructured. The team gathered over 3,000 reports from AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, and annotated them by hand. They compared six prompt strategies and six models, from light to state-of-the-art. The authors report metadata extraction accuracy of 75 to 95 percent. Few-shot prompting helped most fields. Light models gave good trade-offs of accuracy, cost, and speed.
arxiv-2603-16918: Kaleva and co-authors interview U.S. women who use generative AI chatbots for sexual and reproductive health information. Use of such chatbots grew after Roe v. Wade was overturned. The team spoke with 18 participants from states with restrictive and non restrictive laws. Many had shared sensitive personal details with chatbots. Named risks included excess data collection, government surveillance, profiling, and use of chats for model training. Most accepted these risks for the perceived utility. Abortion related queries raised the strongest safety concerns, and few used protective steps.
arxiv-2603-17018: Adans, de Leeuw, and McLoughlin study how deformations can break or keep the integrability of a model. They look at nearest neighbour deformations, expanded in a parameter. Four cases emerge. Some deformations break or preserve integrability. Others are integrable only when all orders are kept, as with long range holographic deformations. A subtler case is integrable up to some order but cannot be extended. They work this out for the XXZ spin chain. They find evidence that chaos sets in differently across the cases.
arxiv-2603-17218: Shapira, Tennenholtz, and Reichart show that aligned language models predict what people should do, not what they do. They compare 120 base and aligned model pairs on over 10,000 real human decisions in strategic games. In multi round games like bargaining and negotiation, base models beat aligned ones at predicting human choices by nearly ten to one. The pattern flips in one shot textbook games and simple lottery choices, where aligned models win. The authors read this as a normative bias from alignment.
arxiv-2603-17318: Ono and co-authors analyze molecular dynamics data through distances between covariance matrices. Such simulations yield huge data that are hard to sum up. Their framework compares system states by the distance between their covariance matrices, the second order moments of the data. Reducing that distance matrix to a few traits then characterizes each system. For Lennard-Jones particles, the top trait tracks the diffusion coefficient in a near linear way. On bulk ice and liquid water, the method cleanly splits the two phases.
arxiv-2603-17418: Badmus and Pandey present PowerDAG, an agent system that automates distribution grid analysis. Engineers face long, stateful jobs like power flow and hosting-capacity checks. PowerDAG writes each workflow as a directed acyclic graph. Adaptive retrieval picks the right expert examples for a task. A just-in-time supervisor then checks each action before it runs and blocks bad ones. On held-out queries it reached up to 98 percent success, they report.
arxiv-2603-17818: Bobadilla wrote this thesis on magnetism and charge flow in strongly correlated electron systems. The Hubbard model sits at the center, with dynamical mean-field theory as the main tool. He varies interaction strength, heat, doping, and field to watch spectra shift and rebuild. In a Zeeman field, the antiferromagnet shows odd resistance curves and local jumps in magnetization. A route to spin-polarized flow driven by correlations alone emerges in plain collinear magnets, he finds. Work on iridates and nanoparticle solids rounds out the thesis.
arxiv-2603-17918: Valdivia-Mena and co-authors trace sulfur oxides around the young star Per-emb 50. Streamers of gas fall toward the disk and can shock the inner envelope. NOEMA maps show two sulfur dioxide peaks southwest of the star. The far peak sits blue-shifted against the infall pattern, marking a streamer shock, they argue. The near peak fits shocks where envelope meets disk. Both match slow shocks of three to four kilometers per second.
arxiv-2603-18118: Dong and co-authors present Insight-V++, a multi-agent framework for long-chain visual reasoning in multimodal models. Good long reasoning data for images and video is scarce, and training paths are weak. A data pipeline builds structured reasoning paths with multi-granularity checks and no human labor. A reasoning agent works through long chains while a summary agent judges and distills results. New ST-GRPO and J-GRPO algorithms boost spatial-temporal reasoning and feedback quality.
arxiv-2603-18218: Casadesus and co-authors present a real-time lunar mapping framework built on 3D Gaussian Splatting. Lunar terrain has poor texture, harsh light, and tight compute limits. They benchmark models on synthetic LuPNT data and pick a GRU stereo depth model plus a CNN segmenter. With ground truth poses, a 120-meter traverse rebuilds with about 3 cm height accuracy. The map beats a point cloud baseline without LiDAR and enables new view synthesis.
arxiv-2603-19018: Wang and Amano study how electrons bounced off collisionless shocks can stir whistler waves. They build the electron spread near the shock with a mapping method. They then test which waves that spread can excite. Bounced electrons can drive two wave types that travel in opposed directions. This needs high values of two shock measures at once. At Earth's bow shock, the waves cannot escape upstream, so they pile up in the shock layer. Their scattering may spark fresh waves on the same branch.
arxiv-2603-19118: Del and co-authors study how doubt scores for reasoning models grow with more sampled answers. They test a black-box route that uses stated confidence and self-consistency across samples. Three reasoning models face seventeen tasks in math, science, and humanities. Both signals scale, but self-consistency starts weaker and lags at mid-size budgets. Mixing the two signals helps most. With just two samples, the mix beats either signal alone at far larger budgets. Gains then fade. Math tasks show the best doubt quality and fastest scaling.
arxiv-2603-19718: Nguyen and co-authors tackle lopsided learning when data comes from several modes at once. In real settings each mode can be missing at a different rate. Strong modes then swamp the weak ones during training. Their BALM framework plugs into existing models without changing their design. One module recalibrates single-mode features with global context. A second module rebalances gradients across modes in size and direction. Tests on emotion recognition benchmarks showed steady gains under missing data.
arxiv-2603-20418: Rodriguez and co-authors seek better roughness measures for unidirectional composite tapes. Surface roughness drives how fully tapes bond during consolidation. Standard statistical measures describe topology but miss the contact physics. Their strategy uses rank reduction autoencoders with a linear latent space. A truncated SVD on the latent matrix enforces that structure. The learned modes must rebuild the surface accurately after decoding. They must also support tape classification and contact modeling. This links one descriptor set to both process control and physics.
arxiv-2603-20518: Clark presents MDMx, a unified model for multi-dimensional mortality analysis. Demographers use life tables, fitting tools, and forecasts built separately. Those tools rarely give structurally coherent sex-specific outputs. MDMx unifies all four tasks in one Tucker tensor decomposition. Human Mortality Database tables form a four-way tensor by sex and age. Shared factors keep every output schedule coherent by construction. Clustering yields model life tables along smooth trajectories. A Kalman filter on reduced core matrices handles forecasting.
arxiv-2603-20618: Shan and co-authors present LogFold, a method to compress software logs. Firms keep logs for long spans to trace faults, but log volume grows fast. Past log tools miss patterns inside complex tokens. They also encode all token types in much the same way. LogFold sorts tokens as structured, plain, or static. It mines patterns in structured tokens and encodes each type to fit. On 16 public log sets it beat prior tools. The gain in ratio averaged 11.11 percent.
arxiv-2603-21118: Kornev introduces a new class of formal group laws tied to the Buchstaber genus. These one dimensional commutative laws have a simple formal inverse, and their modulus square construction yields Buchstaber's polynomials. He proves one law in the class is universal over a stated ring. He computes the genus on theta divisors and projective spaces, and relates it to the Ochanine, Krichever, and Witten genera. A matching cohomology theory is built. The results settle a Hurwitz integrality claim from Bunkova's conjecture.
arxiv-2603-21218: Gonzalez-Espinoza and co-authors study a holographic dark energy model based on Kaniadakis entropy. The model deforms the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy law. This yields a dark energy density with an infrared correction term. With apparent horizon thermodynamics, they derive a geometric equation of state. It shows Van der Waals type criticality, which they read as a phase change of the horizon itself. Tests against supernova, chronometer, and DESI data strongly disfavor the minimal model. An extended model fits best by likelihood but still trails the standard model.
arxiv-2603-21518: Liu and Zhang study the discriminant locus of a generic projection of a smooth projective variety. Working over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, they prove a duality result. The discriminant locus is projectively dual to a general linear section of the dual variety. From this they deduce a purity statement for the discriminant. Over the complex numbers, they also treat a normal hypersurface. There, the fundamental group of the branch divisor's complement maps onto a braid group through braid monodromy.
arxiv-2603-21918: Riso and Zoia build measures of concentration that see both weights and network ties. Classic indices like Herfindahl-Hirschman track weight spread, but ignore who links to whom. Their baseline Network Concentration Index asks what share of possible weighted links the real network carries. Variants then adjust for density, degree limits, null models, data transforms, and layered networks. The family keeps clean traits like normalization and invariance. Tests show systems with equal weights can differ sharply in concentration once topology enters.
arxiv-2603-22218: Nakazato builds an angle measure for affine geometry, a setting where angles are usually absent. He fixes two directions on the line at infinity. The angle between directions is then set by an area cross ratio. It stays fixed under affine maps that keep the chosen directions. Nakazato shows the points that see a fixed segment under one set angle form a hyperbola. This mirrors the Euclidean fact that such points form a circle. The angle also appears in a power theorem for hyperbolas.
arxiv-2603-22318: Padiyar and co-authors shrink chemical reaction mechanisms for combustion with graph neural networks. Full simulations of turbulent flames track hundreds of species and thousands of reactions. That detail makes the runs far too costly. Their networks use message-passing transformer layers to learn links among species and reactions. One version, GNN-SM, leans on a pre-trained surrogate and matches the standard DRGEP method. The other, GNN-AE, uses an autoencoder and cuts species and reactions by up to 95 percent. Tests cover methane, ethylene, and iso-octane mechanisms.
arxiv-2603-22618: Huang, Stodolska, and Sultana examine how people get emotional support from AI companion chatbots. Earlier work mostly measured outcomes, with mixed findings. This study looks at how support is built during the chat itself. The authors study Reddit threads where users discuss AI companions. They find support is co-built through validation, reflective prompts, and companionship. Tension arises between support and dependency, and between validation and delusion. Community replies also shape whether AI care counts as real. The authors frame such support as a negotiated social and technical process.
arxiv-2603-23118: Tu and co-authors study why multimodal language models fail on hidden-pattern visual illusions. People see the hidden content at once, but models miss it. The team built IlluChar, a hard illusion dataset for this test. They trace the failure to a high-frequency attention bias. Background textures distract the models from the hidden pattern. Their fix, SMSP, reshapes images at many scales to suppress that noise. All tested models improve a lot with SMSP. One model's accuracy jumps from near one in eight to over four in five.
arxiv-2603-23218: Julio-Batalla studies a zero mode equation for spinors on closed spin manifolds with positive scalar curvature. A real one-form A plays the role of a magnetic field in the equation. He proves that any nontrivial solution obeys a strict lower bound on the size of dA. The bound is stated through the manifold's Yamabe constant and the dimension. For the round sphere, the result shows that an earlier inequality by Frank is not sharp.
arxiv-2603-23318: Lassance and De Bock widen a way to judge when a classifier's call can be trusted. Robustness scores ask how much uncertainty a model can absorb before its call flips. Past versions needed generative models or narrow setups, which limited their reach. The pair propose a new metric that works for any probabilistic discriminative classifier. It also handles any feature type. Tests show the metric separates reliable calls from shaky ones. They use it to build new rules for picking classifiers on the fly.
arxiv-2603-23418: Li and three co-authors fit the shapes of several BESIII cross sections to pin down charmonium-like states. They study electron-positron collisions that yield strange-charm pairs and J/psi channels. A joint chi-squared fit uses four resonant structures: psi(4230), psi(4500), psi(4660), and psi(4710). The fit returns the mass and width of each state. Three of the channels turn out to be made mostly through psi(4660) and psi(4710) decays. The joint fit ties the separate line shapes into one consistent picture.
arxiv-2603-23618: Kulathunga and three co-authors design beams for cell-free networks that sense and talk at once. Classic solvers for this beam design scale poorly. Learning methods miss the wide links among access points, users, and targets. Their STCIB framework uses a Set Transformer to model those links directly. It treats inputs as unordered sets and trains with no labels. Three modes cover sensing-first, talk-first, and joint goals. Against a CNN, STCIB lifts rates by margins at near-equal runtime. Against classic solvers, it slashes cost with gains.
arxiv-2603-23718: Mantri and five co-authors test hollow-core fiber as a lever for quantum networks. Fresh repeater studies favor multiplexed two-way designs for long links. The team swap plain silica fiber for anti-resonant hollow-core fiber in those designs. They score both media at telecom and memory-native tones, with conversion and memory losses counted. Hollow-core fiber wins across a wide span of regimes. At native tones it lifts secret key rates up to tenfold. Wider repeater spacing also cuts hardware needs.
arxiv-2603-23818: de Teramond and co-authors build a spectral generator for hard exclusive amplitudes in holographic QCD. Their tower of amplitudes assumes a Poisson spread of Fock-state parts. One parameter, fixed by the pion charge radius, sets the average parton count above the valence state. The generator yields a Regge spectrum that stays fixed under smooth changes of that parameter. Its projections give meson and baryon form factors across momentum transfer. The same structure also yields counting rules and a compact form for parton distributions.
arxiv-2603-24118: Zhao and co-authors present S4CMDR, a metadata repository for electronic health records. Health record standards differ by country and hospital, which blocks large shared studies. Their open-source system catalogs data elements, value domains, and compatibility. It builds on the ISO 11179-3 standard and a middle-out approach. Automated cataloguing cuts errors and helps find compatible feature sets across registries. Case studies use rare disease data from the Screen4Care project. The system runs on local Linux servers or in the cloud.
arxiv-2603-24218: Dehghan and McDonald study whether retrieval-augmented generation treats query groups fairly. Such systems ground answers in retrieved documents, which lifts accuracy. The authors test three factors: how often each group's documents are retrieved, how much they help accuracy, and how much the generator relies on them. They use datasets from the TREC 2022 Fair Ranking Track for article and title generation. RAG systems widen accuracy gaps between query groups versus a plain model, they find. All three factors correlate with the gaps.
arxiv-2603-24518: Guan and co-authors present TuneShift-KD, a method for moving specialised knowledge from a fine-tuned model into a newer base model. The original training data is often unavailable, for privacy or commercial reasons. Their key signal is perplexity: prompts where the fine-tuned model is confident but the base model struggles mark the specialised knowledge. TuneShift-KD uses a few such examples to build a synthetic training set. That set then distils the knowledge into the target model automatically, without access to the source data.
arxiv-2603-24618: Hussain and co-authors apply causal inference to analog-mixed-signal circuit design. Such circuits are nonlinear, and data-driven models often miss how design choices drive real performance. Their framework first learns a directed acyclic graph from SPICE simulation data, then estimates average treatment effects for each parameter. The output is an interpretable ranking of design knobs plus what-if predictions. Tested on three amplifier families in a 65 nanometre process, the causal model matches simulation effects within 25 percent error. A neural network baseline errs by over 80 percent.
arxiv-2603-24918: Chen and Wang study how a third-nearest-neighbour Heisenberg interaction affects the Kitaev spin liquid. Evidence for it in candidate Kitaev materials motivates the work. Using a parton mean-field plus random-phase framework, they compute the spin structure factor and Raman response. The added interaction creates paramagnon-like modes beside the Majorana continuum. As the interaction grows, these modes soften and signal a transition to magnetic order. The critical strength is the same for both signs of the coupling, and the ordered states form exact dual pairs.
arxiv-2603-25218: Chen and co-authors build a drone spotter for ground-to-air watch on small hardware. Tiny drones fill few pixels and hide in cluttered skies, so general detectors miss them. SDD-YOLO adds a high-resolution head that works at quarter scale to catch fine detail. It borrows a lean YOLO26 design that skips two slow post steps. A hybrid training plan steadies learning on sparse targets. The team also built a 30,000-image set across weather types. The nano model beats its baseline by 7.8 points of mAP.
arxiv-2603-25318: Somogyvári and Reich let a data filter change its own size while it tracks a moving system. Classic methods fix the model shape and only tune its values. But the right size may be unknown, or may need to shift over time. Their transdimensional particle filter borrows jump moves from reversible-jump sampling. Those moves refresh the particle set and can add or drop state parameters mid-run. The method also trims wasted complexity on its own. Two small model cases show it working.
arxiv-2603-25518: Bai, Touboul, and Fai model how a two-state protein switch can keep a cell's rhythm steady. Cargo proteins flip between two phosphorylation states before they enter the nucleus. That bistable step, joined with transport and growth, can birth oscillations through Hopf bifurcations. Where the flip threshold sits, and how fast parts move, decide the rhythm's fate. Noise then gets added to the model. Stochastic resonance, with a Bautin twist, can shore up the beat instead of wrecking it.
arxiv-2603-25818: Dutta and co-authors explore what the SBND detector could find by running off-target. SBND is a Fermilab neutrino detector. Pointing its beam off target cuts neutrino backgrounds sharply, and a beam-dump setup cuts them further. The authors argue this opens a window on dark sector physics. They project sensitivity to light dark matter and axion-like particles. Heavy neutral leptons and meson-portal cases are covered too. MiniBooNE ran a similar mode before, with leading results.
arxiv-2603-25918: Kamp and co-authors report a new companion star next to the Be star HD 52244. They found it with Hubble's Fine Guidance Sensors. In fall 2021, Hubble paused normal work, and the team used the sensors for a survey of six Be stars. The companion sits 42.7 milliarcseconds away, about 74 astronomical units. Its position angle is 144.2 degrees. It is 1.91 magnitudes fainter in the F583W filter. The study sets up future searches for wide or third companions of Be stars.
arxiv-2603-26018: Abraham and co-authors present GeoReFormer, a transformer for finding lane segments and their links. Online maps for self-driving need accurate 3D lanes plus correct topology. Lane segments are long polylines in directed graphs, unlike compact objects. Standard decoders ignore that structure. GeoReFormer builds geometric priors into its queries. It refines points inside bounded steps for stable shapes. A per-query gate controls how much relational context flows in. On OpenLane-V2, it reaches 34.5 percent mAP, the authors report. Topology consistency also beats strong baselines.
arxiv-2603-26118: Vatré and co-authors measure phase coherence in ultracold bosons trapped in one-dimensional lattices. The team reads the single-particle correlation function from momentum data. Tensor-network simulations of the Bose-Hubbard model include the real lab settings. Deep in the Mott regime, data match near-zero-temperature behavior. At shallow depths, warmth matters more. Fits give an effective temperature that drops as the lattice deepens. The authors read this as blocked heat flow from Mott domains, not true cooling.
arxiv-2603-26718: Abram analyses how to evaluate multi-agent scientific AI systems fairly. Such systems blur the line between reasoning and retrieval, and face contamination risks in their test data. Novel research questions often lack a trusted ground truth, while tool use and shifting knowledge bases complicate repeats. He discusses building tasks that resist contamination and scale in families. Multi-turn tests that mirror real research practice get special weight. A pilot dataset of fresh research ideas, plus interviews with quantum scientists, grounds the proposals.
arxiv-2603-26918: Doyle and co-authors use laser ARPES to track tuning in bismuth selenide-telluride topological insulators. Swapping selenium for tellurium changes the crystals' structure step by step. More tellurium lowers the chemical potential and the Dirac point binding energy. It also thins the density of states from the bulk band. Transport then shifts from metallic toward a semiconducting trend as temperature varies. At the highest tellurium content, resistivity nearly flattens when cold. That plateau signals conduction led by topological surface states.
arxiv-2603-27218: Marmoret tests whether generic deep audio embeddings can reveal musical structure without labels. Music structure analysis is usually taught, but labels are scarce and section edges are ambiguous. Nine open pre-trained models supply bar-level embeddings for the test. Three unsupervised segmentation methods then hunt for section boundaries. Modern ones beat spectrogram baselines, though not in every case. Correlation block matching proved the strongest segmentation method overall. The unsupervised pipeline also topped recent linear probing baselines. Marmoret urges trimming labels to stop padding standard metrics.
arxiv-2603-27518: Maskey and co-authors probe why aligned models refuse safe requests too often. Such over-refusal blocks prompts that merely look harmful. A single global refusal direction seems like a fix. Their tests show harmful refusal is task-free and global. Over-refusal instead lives inside each benign task cluster. Those directions vary by task and span more dimensions. Probing shows the two types split early in the network. Task-specific fixes are thus needed, not one global steer.
arxiv-2603-27718: Battey and Reid rethink how complex models get assessed. Semiparametric fits often blur estimation and assessment steps. Smoothing choices drive much of that blur. Their approach induces replication inside the fitted model. Fisher-style separations split signal from noise parts. Within-sample prediction error then grades the model. Examples cover hazard models and Poisson processes. Matched-pair designs also fit the frame. The method sidesteps kernel tuning woes.
arxiv-2603-27818: Liu and Shen benchmark bird's-eye detection with mixed camera types. Self-driving stacks now pair pinhole and fisheye lenses. Most BEV models assume pinhole views alone. Fisheye warp then degrades their output. KITTI-360 is converted into nuScenes format for tests. Three fixes face trials: rectification, distortion-aware modules, and polar form. BEVFormer, BEVDet, and PETR serve as test models. Projection-free designs prove most robust to warp.
arxiv-2603-27918: Jain and co-authors survey adversarial attacks on multimodal language models. These models fuse text, image, audio, and video streams. That fusion opens fresh attack surfaces. Their taxonomy sorts attacks by attacker objective. A second lens ties attacks to shared weaknesses. Integrity, jailbreak, hijack, and poisoning groups are covered. Architecture and representation flaws recur across groups. The frame guides more robust system design.
arxiv-2603-28518: Shen and four co-authors rewrite the many-body dispersion model so its forces split cleanly into atom pairs. A correlation matrix that scales dipole-dipole coupling does the trick. From it they derive joined formulas for the model's energy, force, and Hessian. The split gives an honest atom-atom reading of a force that is truly many-body. That reading suits both physical analysis and machine learning stand-ins for the full model.
arxiv-2603-28718: Savani and co-authors improve credit assignment for GRPO on flow-matching models. Flow-GRPO gives every step the same credit, based only on the final image. Early steps set composition, while late steps add detail, so uniform credit can reward bad early steps. Their Stepwise-Flow-GRPO credits each step by its reward improvement. It uses Tweedie's formula for intermediate reward estimates and gain-based advantages. A DDIM-inspired stochastic equation improves reward quality while keeping randomness for policy gradients.
arxiv-2603-29118: Gautam and co-authors study how people learn generative 3D modeling tools. They ran an observational study with 26 users, both casual users and professionals. Participants skipped tutorials and manuals. They learned by trial and error instead. The prompt box became the entry point for learning. Some casual users asked outside language models to write their prompts. Professionals judged outputs more strictly and often discarded weak models. Casual users more often settled for good enough results.
arxiv-2603-29318: Nie and co-authors present PSPA-Bench, a benchmark for personalized smartphone agents. Phone agents act through app interfaces, but real use is highly personal. Older benchmarks miss this personal side. PSPA-Bench holds over 12,855 personalized instructions. They span ten daily scenarios and 22 mobile apps. A structure-aware method scores the agent's process in fine detail. The team tested 11 leading agents. Even the strongest agent had limited success. Reasoning models, perception, and memory stood out as key gaps.
arxiv-2603-29518: Vázquez and Torres study whether richer inputs improve language generation for dialogue systems. Generation engines turn meaning representations into sentences. These inputs encode the dialogue act and slot-value content. Their twist adds a task demonstrator: one example pair from the dataset. The enriched input is used in training and at run time. They test five metrics across four datasets with varied domains. Enriched inputs helped most on complex tasks and small, varied datasets. Semantic metrics judged quality better than lexical ones.
arxiv-2603-29818: Erraji, Perrot, and Bellet target fairness in federated learning with unlike clients. Clients join to do better on rare local data, yet still judge the shared model at home. The team defines fairness through the loss gap: global loss minus best local loss. Their EAGLE method shrinks gaps between clients. It favors clients farthest from their local best. They prove convergence for non-convex losses. Tests keep utility competitive with strong baselines.
arxiv-2603-30018: Yang and co-authors present NLSTEM, a denoising step that lifts 4D-STEM pattern indexing. Orientation and phase mapping quantify microstructure fast, but beam precession adds cost and blurs resolution. Their method borrows non-local pattern averaging from electron backscatter work. Patterns get averaged by a distance similarity rule, then reindexed. On nickel and gold films, indexing rates climb markedly. Gains peak in heavily ion-damaged samples. Cleaner signal-to-noise ratios drive the improvement.
arxiv-2604-00118: Naves, Kvorning, and Larson challenge the use of Lindblad spectra as a chaos diagnostic for open quantum systems. They argue that the Hamiltonian analogy breaks down, since late-time behavior depends only on eigenvalues with small real parts. Strong non-normality lets level statistics shift almost freely without changing short- or long-time dynamics. They exhibit cases with Ginibre level repulsion but no chaotic signatures at any time, tying the instability to boundary-driven eigenvector localization resembling a non-Hermitian skin effect.
arxiv-2604-00218: Besanson formalizes the data hydration gap: when ownership decentralizes, each domain team serves its own needs and underinvests in cross-domain generality for reuse. In his game, domains choose quality and generality, where generality helps others but costs its owner. The Nash equilibrium gap grows as domains multiply and cross-domain analytics gain value, and in plausible settings no reusable silver layer emerges, the data mesh trap. Narrow technical debt grows with the square of the domain count, and the model shows when centralized, federated, and hybrid governance dominate.
arxiv-2604-00518: Zhang and colleagues ask whether a deployed agent forum sustains challenge, repair, and public correction, or merely mimics those norms. Comparing Moltbook, a live agent forum, with five matched Reddit communities, they find Moltbook threads branch roughly ten times less, leaving far fewer openings for challenge and reply. When a challenge does land, the first author almost never comes back, multi-turn continuation is nearly absent, and no direct repairs appear on the agent side. The breakdown sits at re-engagement, since the few returning authors often repair substantively.
arxiv-2604-00618: Paryev studies inclusive photoproduction of heavy charmonium chi-c1(1P) from nuclei near threshold. Working in the collision model built on the nuclear spectral function, he treats incoherent direct photon-nucleon creation processes. The model accounts for absorption of the produced charmonium in nuclear matter, plus target nucleon binding and Fermi motion. He computes absolute and relative excitation functions on carbon-12 and tungsten-184 targets at near-threshold photon energies from 8.25 to 16 GeV, along with momentum cross sections and transparency ratios at 13 GeV.
arxiv-2604-00818: Liu and colleagues study how large language models pick up misconceptions, comparing a student model trained on one misconception with a tutor model trained on several. Using their MalAlgoLib library of algebra problems with correct and misconception-laden solution traces, they find the student model overapplies its single error. The tutor model juggles several without losing correct-solving accuracy. A key bottleneck is intermediate reasoning: final-answer supervision alone teaches neither model where errors enter.
arxiv-2604-00918: Martirosyan and colleagues analyze spectral graph neural networks via the graph Fourier transform, where each layer acts as a frequency update element by element, separating the fixed spectrum from trainable parameters. They show Gaussian complexity stays invariant under the Graph Fourier Transform, enabling data-dependent, depth- and order-aware generalization bounds plus stability estimates. In the linear case their bounds tighten. On real graphs the data-dependent term tracks the generalization gap across polynomial bases, guiding choices that avoid frequency amplification across layers.
arxiv-2604-01418: Krumdick and colleagues argue benchmarking quality should be judged by how it predicts performance on unseen tasks. They collect WILD, response pairs covering 65 models on 109564 items spanning 163 tasks from 27 datasets. Combining a multidimensional item response theory model with adaptive item selection, they predict performance on 112 held-out tasks. Error stays under 7 percent after observing 16 items. Adding cost-aware discount factors to selection cuts tokens to reach 7 percent error from 141000 to 22000. That cuts evaluation cost by 85 percent.
arxiv-2604-01618: Chen and colleagues present Tex3D, the first method tuning 3D attack textures end-to-end. Standard 3D sims lack a gradient path from the vision-language-action goal to object look. They present Foreground-Background Decoupling for gradient texture optimization via dual-render matching in the same world. They propose Trajectory-Aware Adversarial Optimization, picking key frames and calming tuning with vertex settings. Tests in sims and real robots show Tex3D hurts vision-language-action results across handling tasks, with task failure rates of up to 96.7 percent.
arxiv-2604-01818: Zhao and colleagues use black hole interior geometry to probe phase changes, instead of horizon thermodynamics. For scalarized AdS black holes, the Kasner exponent tracks the singularity approach across the transition. On one side it swings with temperature amid violent interior motion, while on the other it varies smoothly and calmly. The two sides meet near the critical point, beyond it the exponent forms a peak marking a Kasner crossover line independent of Widom and Frenkel lines. A change in large-scale state reshapes the deepest structure.
arxiv-2604-02418: Storfer and colleagues present Keck adaptive optics imaging of lensed supernova 2025wny, nicknamed Winny. It is the first lensed Type I superluminous supernova in a galaxy scale system for time delay cosmography. Precise positions of its five multiple images constrain lens mass models built with lenstronomy and Glee, using singular isothermal ellipsoid and sphere forms plus external shear. The two models agree and match image positions to sub milli arcsecond residuals. Inferred velocity dispersion for the primary lens, near 277 km/s, matches a DESI value near 298 km/s.
arxiv-2604-02518: Promyslov adds to earlier work on the integro-differential equation behind the ruin problem for annuity payment models with investments. He proves that viscosity solutions, a broad notion of solution for such equations, exist. He then shows they are smooth enough to count as classical solutions. The note is short and technical, closing a gap in the study of the annuity model.
arxiv-2604-02618: Li and three colleagues present OntoKG, a way to build knowledge graphs in which the schema is designed up front for analysis and reuse, rather than emerging from pipeline code. Their intrinsic-relational routing sorts every property as intrinsic or relational and sends it to the matching schema module. Applied to the January 2026 Wikidata dump, the method isolates a 34.6-million-entity core set across 94 modules in 8 groups.
arxiv-2604-03218: Ram and Ramdas study sequential tests that must reject with certainty under every alternative, at a fixed error level. They show a single such test exists for the whole complement whenever the null class is weakly compact, via an information-projection condition. They also show the condition is sufficient but not necessary, and they build an e-process that is asymptotically optimal in growth rate under weak compactness.
arxiv-2604-03518: Lobos and Rodulfo study a Schwarzschild black hole in Modified Gravity shaken by a scalar wave breathing mode. They derive damped, swinging motion for the scalar strain and show surface gravity and changing heat shift in step with the shake's size and speed. First-order shape changes can be undone, while lasting entropy growth is strictly second-order, keeping the Generalized Second Law, and the fading hole is driven toward a stable remnant.
arxiv-2604-03618: Hung-Chun Tsui introduced u-bracket and u-multiple zeta values through the Carlitz module, as function-field cousins of classical q-analog theory. Tsui proved that limits of finite multiple harmonic u-series at Carlitz torsion points recover Thakur's multiple zeta values and finite multiple zeta values. The work also yields explicit relations among Thakur's values at positive and non-positive indices.
arxiv-2604-03718: Junnosuke Koizumi and Ye Liu defined two new invariants for real hyperplane arrangements, built by treating the tope graph as a metric space. In plain terms, they turned a geometric object into numbers and groups that capture its shape. They proved a symmetry formula, palindromic numerator and denominator, a face decomposition, and sign patterns for the power series. The homology detects Boolean arrangements. The Euler characteristic obeys a reciprocity law like the Ehrhart-Macdonald law. The paper closes with conjectures, including torsion-freeness.
arxiv-2604-04118: Vishal Routh and Shuyang Bai introduced the Heavy-Tailed Homogeneous Structural Causal Model, a unified frame for causal discovery under heavy-tailed noise. In such systems, extreme events carry key information about causal direction. They showed that causal tail coefficients identify the full ancestral partial order of the directed acyclic graph. A recursive algorithm then yields ancestral impulse-responses from those coefficients, giving a general, theory-backed frame for causal discovery in heavy-tailed systems.
arxiv-2604-04218: Bonnerjee, Lou and Wu sharpen the theory of Q-learning, a method for learning policies. They study learning rates that decay linearly or as a power law to zero. For this schedule family, the paper proves a tight non-asymptotic error bound. A central limit result follows for a tail-averaged estimator. A time-uniform Gaussian approximation rounds out the results, supporting bootstrap inference. Numerical tests back the theory, which explains why these schedules combine fast early progress with lasting convergence.
arxiv-2604-04418: Zhu and colleagues define error verifiability: whether model justifications help users tell correct answers from wrong ones. The team offers the v-bal metric, testing whether reasons let raters assess correctness, checked against human raters showing high accord. Neither post-training and model scaling nor targeted interventions improve it. Two methods succeed: reflect-and-rephrase for mathematical reasoning and oracle-rephrase for factual QA, both adding domain-fitting external information. The results make error verifiability a distinct quality dimension, not arising from accuracy gains alone, needing focused, domain-aware methods.
arxiv-2604-05018: Song and three co-authors introduce PaperOrchestra, a multi-agent tool for AI research paper writing. Turning raw research materials into papers is key yet under-explored in AI-driven discovery. Existing autonomous writers are tied to specific test pipelines and produce thin reviews. PaperOrchestra flexibly turns free-form pre-writing materials into ready-to-submit LaTeX manuscripts, with full literature surveys and visuals such as plots and diagrams. To test it, the authors present PaperWritingBench, built from raw materials of 200 top-tier AI conference papers.
arxiv-2604-05218: Zhou, Yang, and Chen find rank deficiency of the Hamiltonian in a fragmented model drives quantum Hilbert space fragmentation. Rank deficiency creates local null directions generating entangled frozen states, embedded in mobile Krylov sectors that do not evolve. With a non-empty entangled frozen subspace, the mobile sector splits into a quantum Krylov subspace and an entangled frozen subspace. The mechanism is shown in four models of increasing symmetry. They introduce weak and strong quantum fragmentation: weak-case block counts stay O(1) with GOE statistics.
arxiv-2604-05618: Blanco-Chacón, Dieulefait, and Haavikko derive an explicit formula for Hecke eigenvalues of Hilbert modular forms that lift classical newforms to totally real fields. The lifted form's L-function factors into twists of the original over Galois representations. The same formula proves Hida families lift to formal power series specializing to base-change lifts.
arxiv-2604-05718: Ravé, Rasti, and Rousseau speed up vision transformers for segmentation with Mutual Pair Merging, a training-free token module. It pairs mutual nearest neighbors in cosine space, averages each pair, and rebuilds dense features before the decoder via a merge map. On ADE20K it cuts per-image latency by up to 60 percent on Raspberry Pi 5 and lifts H100 throughput by up to 20 percent with small accuracy loss.
arxiv-2604-05918: Louyer and five colleagues watch pull between millimeter grains in a flat soap film, a far-reaching kin of the Cheerios effect. Film bend that spans the whole setup drives twisty paths lasting up to ten seconds before grains meet. Pull breaks evenness in push and size by up to 150 percent off-center, with even pull back only near the film hub.
arxiv-2604-06218: Chanenson and nine colleagues study how people experience online financial scams and what help they need before, during, and after. They identify the main emotions scammers exploit, such as fear and hope, and show how scammers wield them. Money troubles and legal precarity raise the risk of falling for particular scams and suffering harm. The work traces when people seek help and what they need at each stage, pointing toward tailored prevention, diagnostic, mitigation, and recovery interventions.
arxiv-2604-06318: Pandya and twenty colleagues offer sapphire, a modular, differentiable, GPU-run galaxy formation model in JAX. They compute exact Jacobian grids of a galaxy formation model for the first time. These allow fast sensitivity analyses, showing star-blast energy loading as the key parameter. Fitted factors suggest systems self-control star growth mainly through blocking rather than outward feedback, though doubt remains. Fisher and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo outlooks show its promise for precision inference for galaxy growth and cosmology.
arxiv-2604-06418: Alkhamees, Alfageeh, Alkhazi, Alshdaifat, and Alipour study trust in AI among Middle East computer science students, repeating a United States study in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Jordan. Earlier work drew mostly on Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic populations, so its lessons may not travel. Language fluency predicts trust, and unlike the United States pattern, where females trusted AI more than males, Saudi females trusted it less, with no clear gender gap elsewhere. English skill tracks lower confidence, so adoption work must fit the region's cultural and language needs.
arxiv-2604-06718: Cao and five colleagues model shopping rhythms for next-basket repurchases. Most models read purchase history as visit-ordered events, missing elapsed time and shifting ranks as days pass. CASE treats each item's history as a calendar-time signal, applies shared multi-scale convolutions for rhythms, and uses induced set attention for cross-item ties at sub-quadratic cost. It tops baselines on precision, recall, and NDCG across three benchmarks and a proprietary set. Production tests show about 9 percent precision lift and about 10 percent recall lift at top five.
arxiv-2604-06818: Khosh-Ahang Ghasr bounds Roman and strong Roman k-domination numbers for connected graphs. Motivated by defending networks with legions of varied strength, Roman k-domination and its strong version generalize Roman, double Roman, Italian, and double Italian domination to any legion count. The note sets sharp upper bounds for both numbers on connected graphs, unifying and extending earlier results for k equal to 2 and 3. It also characterizes exactly which graphs attain the bounds.
arxiv-2604-07218: Lei and three colleagues make quantum optimization for vehicle routing more feasible by respecting constraints from the start. Standard QAOA struggles because valid routes fill only a tiny corner of the search space and the usual mixer can break partial solutions. Their framework seeds the initial state with simple local one-hot constraints and uses a hybrid mixer that preserves those constraints while exploring the rest. Across ideal, sampled, and noisy tests, it beats standard QAOA on energy and feasible-solution rates, though the noisy advantage narrows.
arxiv-2604-07518: Zhu, Cheng, and Zhao propose Decompose, Look, and Reason, a reinforced latent reasoning framework for vision-language models that lose visual detail in textual chains of thought. DLR splits queries into text premises, extracts premise-conditioned continuous visual codes, and deduces answers through grounded rationales. A three-stage training pipeline plus a novel Spherical Gaussian Latent Policy enables effective exploration in latent space. On vision-centric benchmarks, DLR consistently beats strong baselines, including text-only, interleaved multimodal chain-of-thought, and latent reasoning methods, while giving superior stepwise interpretability.
arxiv-2604-08118: Kennedy and Moosavi show codebook initialization dominates extreme language-model quantization with additive quantization. This coding enables extreme shrinking with constant-time lookup for edge use. Yet at 2-bit precision it often fails badly, even with long search and tuning. Greedy stepwise initialization often lands the model in poor regions that beam search and PV-tuning struggle to escape. The team studies this behavior through the size ratio rho, linking weight groups to codebook size, and offers OA-EM, an output-aware EM start with Hessian-weighted Mahalanobis distance.
arxiv-2604-08218: Vitali-Derrien and 16 colleagues report giant photostriction in a lead-free ferroelectric driven by thermalized carriers. Ferroelectrics are polar materials with switchable polarization under fields, giving unique chances for strong light-shrinking matter deforming under visible light. Lacking mirror balance by nature, they show new light-driven effects like the Bulk Photovoltaic Effect, driven by hot excited carriers. Workers have long thought this field may join their natural piezoelectric powers to yield large light-driven shape changes. However, rival effects include thermal swelling, warping drive, and field screening.
arxiv-2604-08518: Pike and nine colleagues present a new kind of Fresnel zone plate that joins sharp static focusing with dynamic control for atomic waveguides. The plate, equivalent to a donut shaped convex lens, maps local intensity and global phase onto the image plane. Under varied illumination from a spatial light modulator it yields rings, arcs, double rings, phase windings, and ring lattices. The smooth adaptable near field waveguide suits Sagnac interferometry with ultracold atoms.
arxiv-2604-09318: Zhang and Liu bridge language model understanding with Petri-net checking for parallel programs. Recovering parallel structure from source code is hard because resource identity hides behind aliasing and ownership. Their model-first design has a language model build an artifact from a requirement, in a statement-level alias-free form called Cir. A validated Cir artifact translates to a Petri net called Cvn, explored fully, with counter cases mapped back for repair. A goal-reachability check filters repairs that drop behavior, and 9-pattern tests support repeat bug detection.
arxiv-2604-09618: Zhan and three colleagues build HearthNet, an edge system that lets smart-home users speak plain commands instead of hand-assembling rules, dashboards, and integrations. Real deployments break often, with failing devices, while existing agent toolkits assume short sessions. HearthNet runs persistent, role-specialized agents at the home hub, coordinating through MQTT, Git-backed shared state, and root-issued actuation leases. Planning, verification, authorization, and actuation stay separated. Three live demos cover ambiguous commands, conflict tracing, and stale-order rejection.
arxiv-2604-09818: Young and six co-authors show that self-supervised learning from satellite imagery forecasts below-ground ectomycorrhizal fungal richness in varied settings. Their models account for over half the variance in species richness, using about 12,000 field samples from Europe and Asia. Self-supervised features are the most informative group, outperforming climate, soil, and land-cover baselines. The team achieves a 10,000-fold resolution increase, moving from 1-kilometre landscape averages to 10-metre habitat observations. Because satellite observations change over time, they allow tracking below-ground biodiversity across landscapes for the first time.
arxiv-2604-10018: Reinoso and three colleagues extend chain-referral sampling to cover several traits at once. This method reaches hidden groups through their social networks. Older work assumed random recruitment or let only one trait shape who recruits whom. Their framework lets categorical and continuous traits drive recruitment in a Markov model, adapts prevalence estimators, and adds a neighborhood bootstrap for uncertainty. Simulations and a study of Venezuelan adults in Santiago, Chile, test the method.
arxiv-2604-10218: Wang and five colleagues improve self-taught stereo matching with SMFormer, guided by a base model and image tweaks. Self-taught methods assume matching points look alike across views, but real noise breaks that match and leaves invalid guidance. SMFormer pairs the base model with a feature pyramid network for robust cues. Its training tweaks force a match between learned and shifted cues, and steady the match between tweaked and standard depth guesses. SMFormer leads self-taught methods on benchmarks and rivals labeled ones, even beating some on Booster.
arxiv-2604-10318: Ghoshal, Huang, Lee, and the two Makarychevs probe Max-Cut on graphs with mild color limits. Max-Cut splits nodes to cut as many links as possible, a task long known to resist exact answers. They show the classic Goemans Williamson bound stays hard to beat on three color graphs. A sharp cutoff splits graphs by the size of their largest freestanding node set. Past that cutoff, a new relaxation method beats the classic bound for good.
arxiv-2604-10418: Eberbach ties Turing's feats to Cantor's older work on sets and the roots of math. He scores how unsolvable a task is by the share of inputs no Turing machine can settle. Turing's infinite logics and oracle machines grow here into a full class of super Turing models. Three fresh classes sort undecidable tasks: U-complete, D-complete, and H-complete. For U-complete tasks, he settles the twin of the P versus NP query in the negative.
arxiv-2604-10718: Sehwag and colleagues introduce SciPredict, a test of 405 tasks from recent studies in 33 small fields of physics, biology, and chemistry, asking whether language models can predict lab results. Models score only 14 to 26 percent, near the 20 percent of human experts, far below what sound lab guidance needs. Worse, models cannot tell good guesses from bad ones, scoring near 20 percent no matter how sure they seem. Human experts, by contrast, grow far more accurate as they judge an outcome more predictable, rising from 5 percent to 80 percent.
arxiv-2604-10918: Yang and three colleagues propose CSPO, Component-Specific Policy Optimization, a reinforcement learning frame for table-to-LaTeX work that untangles tuning across parts: structure, style, content. Standard post-training uses one lumped reward, blurring behaviors and blocking effective tuning. CSPO gives each part its own reward and sends each signal only through tokens tied to that part, easing ambiguity and enabling targeted part-wise tuning. With layered metrics, broad tests show CSPO works well, underscoring part-wise tuning for reliable structured generation. Code is available on GitHub.
arxiv-2604-11118: Malik, Kargin, and Hassibi harden k-means clustering against outliers and shifting data. Treating clustering as quantization of the observed distribution, they seek centers that minimize the worst-case error over all distributions within a Wasserstein-2 ball around it. A tractable dual turns hard assignments into smooth weights, and a block coordinate descent algorithm converges locally at a linear rate while improving outlier detection in tests.
arxiv-2604-11218: Walther, Giraud, and Clément introduce H-SPAM, a method that builds nested hierarchies of superpixels, coherent pixel groupings, from a fine partition upward. Guided by deep features and object priors, a two-phase merging process first preserves object consistency, then allows controlled grouping across objects, with attention maps or user input able to protect key regions. Benchmarks show it strongly beats hierarchical rivals and matches leading flat methods.
arxiv-2604-11318: Bonnet, Le, and the Pilipczuks give a coarse analogue of the balanced separator theorem for graphs. Fat minors require the pieces modeling an embedded graph to sit far apart, not merely disjoint. They prove every n-vertex graph excluding H as a d-fat minor has a balanced separator coverable by n to the one-half-plus-epsilon balls of fixed radius. The proof also covers vertex weights and yields a randomized polynomial-time algorithm that finds either such a separator or a d-fat model of H.
arxiv-2604-11718: Michetti, Provenzano, and Savo bound the first eigenvalue of the magnetic Laplacian, with no magnetic field, on simply connected compact surfaces, tying it to a limit on Gaussian curvature. Among spherical regions of fixed area, they show the value peaks for a geodesic disk with the magnetic pole at its centre. For a sphere pierced at two points, the peak instead comes when those points sit opposite each other.
arxiv-2604-11818: Santos and Ricardo model arboviral spread in Recife, Brazil, with a probabilistic framework based on pairwise interaction kernels over space and time. They find spatial closeness adds almost no power to separate diseases at city scale, while timing does: dengue, Zika, and chikungunya only become statistically distinct beyond a critical time window. Biologically constrained versions of the model, they argue, reveal a shared transmission structure beneath short-term co-occurrence.
arxiv-2604-12018: Alhazmi and Jiang examine abstract meaning comprehension, where abstract words challenge models through non-concrete, high-level semantics. On SemEval-2021 Task 4, testing abstract concepts via passages, questions, and five abstract cloze options, most large language models, including GPT-4o, struggle under zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot settings. Fine-tuned BERT and RoBERTa do better. Their bidirectional attention classifier, inspired by human cognitive strategies, dynamically attends to passages and options, improving accuracy by 4.06 percent on Task 1 and 3.41 percent on Task 2.
arxiv-2604-12218: Patel benchmarks large language models against classic methods for spotting anomalies in system logs, across four public datasets. Fine-tuned transformers score highest, with F1 from 0.96 to 0.99, while prompt-based models reach 0.82 to 0.91 with no labeled training data at all. That zero-shot strength matters where labeled anomalies are scarce. The study also weighs cost, latency, and failure modes to guide practitioners choosing a method.
arxiv-2604-12318: Inoue and three colleagues frame cell instance segmentation as distribution-based image-to-image generation through a multi-task Schrödinger Bridge. Boundary-aware supervision via a reverse distance map plus deterministic inference yields stable predictions without heavy post-processing. On PanNuke the method matches or beats rivals without SAM pretraining or extra post-processing, and on MoNuSeg it stays robust with limited training data. The bridge framework thus offers an effective route to cell segmentation.
arxiv-2604-12518: Kang He and five colleagues improve multimodal sentiment analysis when some signals go missing. Text, audio, and video signals jointly reveal human emotion. Strong signals often drown weaker ones, hurting fusion quality. Their EBMC framework first strengthens weak signals through disentanglement and cross-modal enhancement. An energy-guided coordination mechanism then rebalances gradients implicitly. Sample-level trust distillation adjusts fusion weights per instance. Tests show leading or competitive results with strong missing-signal performance.
arxiv-2604-12618: Weichuang Zhang and eight colleagues build CODO, a compiler for FPGA dataflow design. Gate arrays suit streaming, pipelined work. Hand design of fast flows stays hard even with high-level synthesis. CODO finds and removes flow faults at coarse and fine grains. It tunes data movement on and off chip for speed. Auto scheduling balances speed against cost. Kernel latency speedups run 1.45 to 4.52 times over leading tools. On-board tests confirm gains on CNN and GPT-2 models.
arxiv-2604-13018: Guoxin Chen and nine colleagues present AiScientist, a multi-agent system that turns vague research goals into tested machine-learning systems. A lightweight hierarchy of agents shares work through a File-as-Bus workspace that preserves decisions across stages, sustaining progress despite delayed and tangled feedback. It beats the strongest matched baselines on PaperBench and reaches 81.82 percent on MLE-Bench Lite, with ablations showing the shared workspace drives later gains.
arxiv-2604-13518: Dutta, Vyas, and Roy study self-taught learning and forward-looking representation learning, naming Predictive Representation Learning as a new class. Current methods align maps and rebuild inputs. They perform well but stay confined to seen data, offering little forward-looking help. That approach instead predicts unseen parts from what is seen. The authors classify it with matching and rebuild work, with Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture as an example. Masked Autoencoders reach perfect likeness but only 55 percent toughness, while the other two reach 98 and 95 percent scores with 75 and 78 percent toughness.
arxiv-2604-13618: Kawabata and Sugawara improve reward models with rubrics, explicit scoring criteria, without paying for rubric annotations. Their C2 framework trains a rubric generator from binary preferences alone. It pairs helpful and misleading rubrics, while a critical verifier accepts only rubrics it judges helpful. The result beats reasoning reward models trained on the same preferences, gaining up to six and a half points in RM-Bench tests. An 8-billion-parameter model then matches rubrics from a model four times larger.
arxiv-2604-13718: Pandey and three colleagues compute the optical depth to reionization in a universe of multiple inhomogeneous domains, using the Buchert averaging formalism with backreaction from matter clumps. Fitting model parameters to the PantheonPlus and SH0ES supernova samples by Markov Chain Monte Carlo, they obtain an optical depth near 0.058. That value matches observational estimates more closely than the standard cosmological model predicts, and the model modestly eases the Hubble tension without exotic physics.
arxiv-2604-14318: König derives a minimum-energy formula for the interacting Bose gas free energy in the large-system limit, tracking particle numbers in short and long loops. Long loops, thought to form the condensate, turn into random interlacements, going beyond earlier work that handled only small densities. The formula ranges over steady point processes with loops and interlacements at fixed density, minimizing interaction energy plus a new specific relative entropy density. In three-plus dimensions, the result links to a Brownian interlacement process, with large-deviation theory proving both.
arxiv-2604-14718: Qi argues that the deepest effect of large language models on science is not faster automation. It is a change in how complex knowledge and know-how are carried, copied, and shared. The essay traces a gradual path from AI as a laboratory tool to AI as a scientific collaborator. That shift, Qi contends, could reshape collaboration, discovery, publishing, and evaluation. Continuous learning and a diversity of ideas are essential if AI is to make genuinely original discoveries. Without them, it would merely speed up existing routines.
arxiv-2604-15118: Kuang and colleagues hunt permission-control flaws in NFT contracts with NFTDELTA, a multi-view learning framework. It reads function control-flow graphs through two lenses: sequence features tracing execution paths and graph features capturing control structure. The fused view feeds a custom detector for three flaw classes, including auth bypass by reentrancy. Tests on 795 popular collections found 241 confirmed flaws at about 98 percent precision.
arxiv-2604-15418: Babel, Saunderson, and Rismani draft a framework that ranks anthropomorphic deception in robots and AI across four levels, where deception means design that misleads users toward humanlike affordances. Four levels, set by humanlikeness, agency, and selfhood, sort designs by whether they are needed to work, fit social norms, and pass ethical muster. The authors urge a balanced view, neither treating humanlike design as a harmless default nor as mere exploitation.
arxiv-2604-15518: Shore derives the rovibrational spectrum of hydrogen and antihydrogen molecular ions in the Standard-Model Extension, a field theory with Lorentz and CPT violation. It is the third paper of a series. New work covers full molecule motion in spherical tensor form, extension to the non-minimal SME, quantum-number patterns at high and low magnetic fields, and sidereal and annual frequency shifts. Sensitivity in principle reaching ten to the minus seventeen sharpens the hunt for symmetry breaking.
arxiv-2604-15618: Launer and four colleagues study functional majority voting for code generation, which picks one answer from many model tries by how each try runs on test inputs. The test-time trick lifts LiveCodeBench scores a lot without much extra compute. Used to combine label-free test-time reinforcement learning, it raises pass-at-1 on holdout tasks but shows no self-gains beyond the base model's ceiling.
arxiv-2604-16018: Christian Schmidt reports on efforts to modernize the International Lattice Data Grid, a shared service for lattice field theory data. Work covers metadata and middleware groups deploying and operating key services, including user management, metadata catalogues, and file catalogues. Format extensions have been tailored to the needs of large teams. The report also looks ahead to planned developments for the foreseeable future.
arxiv-2604-16118: Bachmayr, Krämer, and Pfeffer develop an iterative, rank-adaptive eigensolver for Schrödinger equations that builds low-rank approximations of eigenfunctions, with ranks tuned to the accuracy wanted. Their focus is fermionic equations in second-quantized form, using matrix product states that preserve particle number. They fully analyse a solver pairing preconditioned inverse iteration with rank truncation, extend it to several eigenspaces at once, and test it on model problems.
arxiv-2604-16218: Gonçalves, Kaladharan, and Navarro study quantum tomography and entanglement in semi-leptonic Higgs decays to electroweak gauge bosons. Angular patterns in such decays probe new physics and quantum information alike. They include finite fermion masses and next-to-leading-order QCD and electroweak corrections. Quark masses can push the picture beyond a two-qutrit description in inclusive regimes, yet stay controllable with suitable cuts. QCD shifts are modest, electroweak shifts can reshape angles, and semi-leptonic channels still fit the two-qutrit picture better than fully leptonic decays.
arxiv-2604-16318: Lemdiasova and Zmanovskii diagnose LLM-based rankers for cold-start movie picks, where user history is thin. In practice, these rankers lag far behind simple baselines. Using the Serendipity-2018 dataset and careful tests with 500 users, they find three failure modes. Candidate picks cover little, with recall at 200 of 0.109 against 0.609 for baselines. Rankers also concentrate on just 3 items against 497 for a random baseline, and barely tell relevant from irrelevant items apart.
arxiv-2604-16418: Digulescu proposes a framework for reasoning about algorithms when input size has a known upper bound, rather than growing without limit. Adapting complexity ideas to this finite setting, he offers results and a method for finding a suitable algorithm for the finite version of a hard problem, where one exists. He argues that finite cases should prove easier than general cases. He sketches ideas for three hard problems: satisfiability in 3CNF form, string compression and integer factorization. The paper is a proposal, not a claimed general solution.
arxiv-2604-16518: Wang surveys on-orbit space AI for satellite constellations, which turn lone craft into linked platforms for sensing and choices. Prior work mostly covers single craft, yet fleet self-control adds learning under shifting links, size-weight-power-cost limits, radiation faults, mixed data, drift and safety constraints. He sorts the field into three routes: federated learning across craft, multi-agent planning, and joint sensing with shared work. A map unifies teamwork designs, time methods and trust models, with a curated paper list kept current.
arxiv-2604-16718: Nadiger and colleagues test quantum approximate optimization for energy-saving route planning. Routing is NP-hard, encoded here as a binary optimization problem. QAOA at depth three to five beats simulated annealing and genetic algorithms on five, ten and twenty nodes. Approximation ratios reach about 95, 92 and 90 percent across those sizes, beating classical baselines by about 3 to 4 percent. QAOA runs two to three times faster than simulated annealing, with energy use down a thousandfold. An 8 percent efficiency gain could save fuel yearly and avoid about 194 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.
arxiv-2604-16918: Ma and six colleagues fix a staleness flaw in experience replay for language-model training. Old high-priority examples keep dominating sampling long after they stop teaching anything. Their freshness-aware variant decays priority exponentially with age, lifting scores by 46 percent on NQ Search, 367 percent on Sokoban, and 133 percent on VLM FrozenLake over on-policy baselines.
arxiv-2604-17018: Andrašek studies rational Diophantine triples where each pair product plus one is a fourth power. He produces non-trivial infinite families of such triples with positive elements for fourth powers. The paper also looks briefly at the sixth- and eighth-power cases, explaining why the method resists extension to higher exponents.
arxiv-2604-17318: Ghosh, Baidya, Saha, and Chen attack medical vision-language models through the background of images, where doctors would not look for disease. Their MedFocusLeak method nudges non-diagnostic background pixels and distracts the model's attention, producing wrong yet plausible diagnoses that transfer across systems without visible distortion. Tested across six imaging types, it exposes a serious weakness in clinical AI reasoning and comes with new measures balancing attack success against image fidelity.
arxiv-2604-17418: Kutak and Lökös use dipole models of high-energy collisions to study entropy and mean particle counts. To dodge differing lab definitions of rapidity ranges, they propose entropy as a function of the log of mean multiplicity as a universal gauge. They compute both quantities from the models and match them to proton-proton data, fitting parameters straight to measured count distributions. The generalized dipole model fits the data far better than the 1D Mueller model.
arxiv-2604-18018: He and twenty-two colleagues describe the trigger and localization system of SVOM's Gamma-Ray Monitor, one of four payloads on the China-France satellite launched on 22 June 2024. The monitor carries three gamma-ray detectors with distinct pointings, covering 15 to 5,000 kilo-electronvolts. The paper presents the on-board localization algorithm with preliminary tests, then a ground-based joint fitting method using Markov chain Monte Carlo that accounts for spectral traits and reduces systematic bias. For GRB 240629A, its localization error of about 4.14 degrees matches the Fermi/GBM result.
arxiv-2604-18318: Zaid and Hertz design tactical wireless networks for places where normal phone service is down or destroyed, such as crisis zones. Such networks must adapt to rough terrain while boosting signal and reach and cutting interference. The authors propose two tabu search methods with rule-of-thumb helpers that build high-quality designs. Lab tests show fast, good networks that beat older methods by a wide margin.
arxiv-2604-18418: Liu and 21 colleagues introduce MedProbeBench, a benchmark for expert-level medical guideline work by deep-research systems. Existing tests miss realistic multi-step evidence integration and expert judgment. The benchmark uses clinical guidelines as references, with holistic rubrics spanning over 1,200 criteria and evidence checks grounded in over 5,130 atomic claims. Tests of 17 language models and research agents expose wide gaps in evidence integration and guideline generation, far from expert-level practice.
arxiv-2604-18718: David and Gervais ask when adding more agents helps agentic security systems that audit live targets with tool-using language models. Their controlled benchmark covers 20 interactive targets, half web or API and half binary, each with one endpoint-reachable flaw, and runs 600 core experiments across architecture and model families. Independent multi-agent systems reach the highest validated detection rate, while a single-agent setup is the cheapest per validated finding. Whitebox access far outperforms blackbox access, and web targets far outperform binary ones.
arxiv-2604-18818: Fekih-Salem extends a three stage anaerobic digestion model by adding microbial mortality to hydrolysis. The model covers hydrolysis, acidogenesis, and methanogenesis, each with its own decay rates, and captures substrate inhibition. Two hydrolysis forms are studied, a first order form and a biomass based form, with the latter splitting washout from mortality. The author proves the solutions are well posed, above zero, and bounded, finds all equilibria, and checks their stability.
arxiv-2604-19018: Skifstad, Yang, and Chou show LLM layer dynamics are locally linear, enabling activation steering by linear optimal control. Current steering uses open loop interventions that ignore perturbation spread across layers and lack error feedback. They model inference as a linear time varying system and adapt the linear quadratic regulator, using layer Jacobians to steer activations to setpoints in closed loop. They also bound tracking error, giving formal steering guarantees. With an adaptive setpoint signal, the method controls toxicity, truthfulness, refusal, and arbitrary concepts, beating baselines.
arxiv-2604-19118: Thompson, Sen, and Bhattacharya propose DP-FLogTinyLLM for private federated log anomaly detection with Tiny models. Logs spread across organizations cannot be pooled for privacy and security, and current methods assume centralized training. Their approach learns jointly without sharing raw logs, using federated optimization with differential privacy. Low rank adaptation fine tunes Tiny models at each client for constrained settings. On Thunderbird and BGL data, it matches centralized methods despite extra compute overhead, and beats other baselines on precision and F1, with its best gains on Thunderbird.
arxiv-2604-19818: Koch and Wellbrock build an evidence-synthesis framework for judging, governing, and orchestrating agentic AI beyond simple task success. Agentic systems plan, use tools, keep state, and act across multi-step workflows with external effects. So task completion alone cannot vouch for trustworthy deployment. Surveying a hand-coded corpus of twenty-four recent sources, they find a governance-to-action closure gap. Evaluation judges outcomes and governance states what is allowed, but neither shows where duties bind to concrete actions or how compliance could be demonstrated afterward.
arxiv-2604-19918: Liveoak, Hallatt, and Millholland ask how destroyed hot Jupiters shape multiplanet stability. The sub-Jovian desert, a sparse zone of worlds with periods under about three days and masses near ten to one hundred Earth masses, may hold such giants' remains. Loss through Roche lobe overflow clears companions inside periods near four days, so desert dwellers formed this way should sit alone. Most observed companions lie safely beyond that zone, while tidal disruption during migration would threaten nearer neighbors, letting observers tell the two fates apart.
arxiv-2604-20218: Chitrao, Jana, and Soneji map invariants of the universal module under the pro-p Iwahori subgroup for two endpoint cases, via the Iwahori-Hecke model. Supersingular representations are the base blocks of mod p matrix group representations over p-adic fields, and these invariants helped build them. They also pin down how the pro-p Iwahori-Hecke algebra acts on the new invariants. As a payoff, they win the module back from its invariants by functorial means and stretch Ollivier's theorem to every totally ramified extension except the field itself.
arxiv-2604-20418: Ghodsi, Kiritsis, and Nitti map the ground states of confining holographic quantum field theories, theories with a gravity dual. They place those theories on constant-curvature spaces with a theta angle, computing free energy and phase structure.
